functions.description: Checks if you have permission to write to a file or update a directory. Uses the current SKILL path for relative paths. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

functions.name: labels
functions.description: Enables you to define local functions with LET semantics.

functions.name: lambda
functions.description: Defines a function without a name. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: last
functions.description: Returns the last list cell in a list.

functions.name: lconc
functions.description: Uses a tconc structure to efficiently splice a list to the end of another list.

functions.name: leftshift
functions.description: Returns the integer result of shifting a value a specified number of bits to the left. Prefix form of the << arithmetic operator. leftshift is logical (that is, vacated bits are 0-filled).

functions.name: length
functions.description: Determines the length of a list, array, association table, or string.

functions.name: leqp
functions.description: This predicate function checks if the first argument is less than or equal to the second argument. Prefix form of the <= operator.

functions.name: lessp
functions.description: This predicate function checks if the first argument is less than the second argument. Prefix form of the < operator.

functions.name: let
functions.syntax: SKILL mode let(  l_bindings  g_expr1 ...  )  => g_result  SKILL++ mode let(  [ s_var ] 	( 		( s_var1 s_initExp1 ) 		( s_var2 s_initExp2 ) 	... 	) body ) => g_result
functions.description: In the SKILL mode, this function provides a faster alternative to prog for binding local variables only. This is a syntax form. In the SKILL++ mode, this function declares a lexical scope. This includes a collection of local variables, as well as body expressions to be evaluated. This becomes a named let if the optional s_var is given.

functions.name: letrec
functions.syntax: letrec( 	( 		( s_var1 s_initExp1 ) 		( s_var2 s_initExp2 ) 	...  	) body )  => g_result
functions.description: (SKILL++ mode) A letrec expression can be used in SKILL++ mode only. All the bindings are in effect while their initial values are being computed, thus allowing mutually recursive definitions. Use letrec to declare recursive local functions.

functions.name: letseq
functions.syntax: letseq( 	( 		( s_var1 initExp1 ) 		( s_var2 initExp2 )  		... 	) body ) => g_result
functions.description: A letseq expression can be used in both SKILL and SKILL++ modes. The bindings and evaluations are performed sequentially.

functions.name: lindex
functions.syntax: lindex(  l_list  g_element  [ ?all g_all ] )  => x_result / l_result / nil
functions.description: Returns the index number of the given element in l_list.

functions.name: lineread
functions.description: Parses the next line in the input port into a list that you can further manipulate. It is used by the interpreter's top level to read in all input and understands SKILL and SKILL++ syntax.

functions.name: linereadstring
functions.description: Executes lineread on a string and returns the first form read in. Anything after the first form is ignored.

functions.name: list
functions.description: Creates a list with the given elements.

functions.name: listAlias
functions.description: Prints a (property) list of all current aliases and associated function symbols, or the function symbol for which the given alias is defined.

functions.name: listFunctions
functions.description: Returns all public function names that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression. If the second (optional) argument is specified as t (or a non-nil value), listFunctions looks at the SKILL virtual machine, rather than the cdsFinder database, and returns all isCallable Cadence public functions and user-defined SKILL functions that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression.

functions.name: listToVector
functions.description: Returns a vector (array) filled with the elements from the given list. A vector is represented by an array.

functions.name: listVariables
functions.description: Returns all variable names that match the given substring or regular expression as part or all of their print name.

functions.name: listp
functions.description: Checks whether the specified object is a list.

functions.name: loadContext
functions.syntax: loadContext(  t_contextFileName  [ g_ignore64bitSubpath ] )  => t / nil / error
functions.description: Loads a context file into the current session.

functions.name: loadPort
functions.syntax: loadPort(  p_port  [?langMode g_langMode] [?password g_password] [?ignoreErrors g_ignoreErrors]) )  => t
functions.description: Loads a SKILL file from p_port.

functions.name: loadTopContextForms
functions.syntax: loadTopContextForms(  t_FileName  [ ?debugMode g_debugMode ]  [ ?writeProtect g_writeProtect ]  [ ?writeProtectAll g_writeProtectAll ]  [ ?lazyComp g_lazyComp ]  [ ?printinfix g_printinfix ]  [ ?integermode g_integermode ]  [ ?mergemode g_mergemode ]  [ ?readProtect g_readProtect ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Loads top-level SKILL or Scheme forms from a file. If the setContext mode is set, these forms are saved in a context. After the context is loaded, these forms are evaluated at the top-level, as if these were loaded from an .il or .ils file.

functions.name: loadi
functions.description: Identical to load, except that loadi ignores errors encountered during the load, prints an error message, and then continues loading.

functions.name: loadstring
functions.description: Opens a string for reading, then parses and executes expressions stored in the string, just as load does in loading a file.

functions.name: lowerCase
functions.description: Returns a string that is a copy of the given argument with uppercase alphabetic characters replaced by their lowercase equivalents.

functions.name: lsprintf
functions.description: Returns a string according to the provided format. lsprintf is a lambda version of the sprintf function that can be used as an argument with apply or funcall.

functions.name: makeInstance
functions.syntax: makeInstance(  us_class  [ u_?initArg1    value1 ] [ u_?initArg2    value2 ] ...  ) => g_instance
functions.description: Creates an instance of a class, which can be given as a symbol or a class object.

functions.name: makeNamespace
functions.description: Creates a SKILL namespace with the given t_name. A namespace or its parts can be saved in a context and loaded with the context.

functions.name: makeSymbol
functions.description: Creates a symbol corresponding to the specified symbol or character string. You can optionally specify the namespace name (t_namespace) in which you want to create the symbol.

functions.name: makeTable
functions.description: Creates an empty association table.

functions.name: makeTempFileName
functions.description: Appends a string suffix to the last component of a path template so that the resulting composite string does not duplicate any existing file name.

functions.name: makeVector
functions.description: Creates an array (vector) with the specified number of elements, and optionally initializes each entry.

functions.name: make_<name>
functions.description: Creates an instance of a defstruct specified by name.

functions.name: map
functions.description: Applies the given function to successive sublists of the argument lists and returns the first argument list. All of the lists should have the same length. This function is not the same as the standard Scheme map function. To get the behavior of the standard Scheme map function, use mapcar instead. This function is usually used for its side effects, not its return value (see mapc).

functions.name: mapc
functions.description: Applies a function to successive elements of the argument lists and returns the first argument list. All of the lists should have the same length. mapc returns l_arg1.

functions.name: mapcan
functions.description: Applies a function to successive elements of the argument lists and returns the result of appending these intermediate results. All of the lists should have the same length.

functions.name: mapcar
functions.description: Applies a function to successive elements of the argument lists and returns the list of the corresponding results.

functions.name: mapcon
functions.description: Applies the function u_func to successive sublists of the lists and returns a concatenated list.

functions.name: mapinto
functions.description: Applies g_function to the elements of l_sequences and destructively modifies the l_resultSequence. The first argument is a sequence that receives the results of the mapping. If l_resultSequence and the other argument sequences are not all of the same length, the mapping stops when the shortest of l_resultSequence or l_sequences is exhausted.

functions.name: maplist
functions.description: Applies a function to successive sublists of the argument lists and returns a list of the corresponding results. All of the lists should have the same length.

functions.name: measureTime
functions.description: Measures the time needed to evaluate an expression and returns a list with performance data (n_utime, n_stime, n_clockTime, and x_pageFaults) for the executed expressions. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: member, memq, memv
functions.syntax: member(  g_obj  g_arg  )  => l_sublist / t / nil
functions.description: Returns the largest sublist of l_list whose first element is g_obj or checks whether the key g_obj exists in the association table. For comparison, member uses the equal function, memq uses the eq function, and memv uses eqv.

functions.name: memoryAllocated
functions.description: Returns the amount of memory allocated by a process. The returned value is an approximation in megabytes and might not include the memory that has been allocated, but the amount that is unused.

functions.name: minus
functions.description: Returns the negative of a number. Prefix form of the - unary operator.

functions.name: minusp
functions.description: Checks if a value is a negative number. Same as negativep.

functions.name: modf
functions.description: Returns the floating-point remainder of the division of f_flonum1 by f_flonum2.

functions.name: modulo
functions.description: Returns the remainder of dividing two integers. The remainder always has the sign of the divisor.

functions.name: mprocedure
functions.description: Defines a macro with the given name that takes a single formal argument. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: muffleWarnings
functions.description: Returns the result of the last expression evaluated. If the last expression evaluated calls the warn function (either SKILL warn() or C-level ilWarn*), the related message is not printed out.

functions.name: nconc
functions.description: Equivalent to a destructive append where the first argument is modified.

functions.name: ncons
functions.description: Builds a list containing an element. This function is equivalent to cons( g_element nil ).

functions.name: nearlyEqual
functions.syntax: nearlyEqual(  n_val1 n_val2  [ f_relTolerance [f_absTolerance] ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Checks whether one value (n_val1) is approximately equal to another value (n_val2).

functions.name: needNCells
functions.description: Ensures that there is enough memory available for the specified number of SKILL objects (cells).

functions.name: negativep
functions.description: Checks whether the specified value is a negative number. Same as minusp.

functions.name: neq
functions.description: Checks if two arguments are not identical using the eq function and returns t if they are not. That is, g_arg1 and g_arg2 are tested to see if they are at the same address in memory.

functions.name: nequal
functions.description: Checks if two arguments are not logically equivalent using the equal function and returns t if they are not.

functions.name: next
functions.description: Allows execution to proceed until the next expression. This function only works if executed from within a break handler and if the code you want to step through was loaded under debugMode. See installDebugger.

functions.name: nextMethodp
functions.description: Checks if there is a next applicable method for the current method's generic function. The current method is the method that is calling nextMethodp.

functions.name: nindex
functions.description: Finds the symbol or string, S_string2, in t_string1 and returns the character index, starting from one, of the first point at which the S_string2 matches part of t_string1.

functions.name: nlambda
functions.description: (SKILL mode only) Allows nlambda functions to be defined without having names. In all other respects, nlambda is identical to nprocedure. This is a syntax form that is not supported in SKILL++ mode.

functions.name: not
functions.description: Same as the ! operator. Returns t if the object is nil, and returns nil otherwise.

functions.name: nprocedure
functions.description: (SKILL mode only) Defines an nlambda function with a function name and a single formal argument. This is a syntax form that is not supported in SKILL++ mode.

functions.name: nth
functions.description: Returns an index-selected element of a list, assuming a zero-based index.

functions.name: nthcdr
functions.description: Applies cdr to a list a given number of times.

functions.name: nthelem
functions.description: Returns the indexed element of the list, assuming a one-based index.

functions.name: null
functions.description: Checks if an object is equal to nil.

functions.name: numOpenFiles
functions.description: Returns the number of files now open and the maximum number of files that a process can open. The numbers are returned as a two-element list.

functions.name: numberp
functions.description: Checks if a data object is a number, that is, either an integer or floating-point number.

functions.name: oddp
functions.description: Checks whether an object is an odd integer. oddp is a predicate function.

functions.name: onep
functions.description: Checks whether the given object is equal to one. onep is a predicate function.

functions.name: openportp
functions.description: Checks if the given argument is a port object and it is open (for input or output), nil otherwise.

functions.name: or
functions.syntax: or(  g_arg1  g_arg2  [ g_arg3... ]  )  => nil / g_val
functions.description: Evaluates from left to right its arguments to see if the result is non-nil. As soon as an argument evaluates to non-nil, or returns that value without evaluating the rest of the arguments. If all arguments except the last evaluate to nil, or returns the value of the last argument as the result of the function call. Prefix form of the || binary operator.

functions.name: otherp
functions.description: Checks if an object is a user type object, such as an association table or a window.

functions.name: outportp
functions.description: Checks if an object is an output port.

functions.name: outstring
functions.description: Takes no arguments and returns an opened output port for strings (or an outport). After a port is opened, it can be used with functions, such as fprintf, println, and close that write to an output port. You need to use the getOutstring function to retrieve the content of output port (while it is open).

functions.name: outstringp
functions.description: Checks whether the specified value is an outstring port.

functions.name: pairp
functions.description: Checks if an object is a cons object, that is, a non-empty list. This function is equivalent to dtpr.

functions.name: parseString
functions.description: Breaks a string into a list of substrings with break characters.

functions.name: pcreCompile
functions.description: Compiles a regular expression string pattern (t_pattern) into an internal representation that you can use in a pcreExecute function call. The compilation method is PCRE/Perl-compatible. You can use a second (optional) argument to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compilation. You can set and unset the PCRE_CASELESS, PCRE_MULTILINE, PCRE_DOTALL, and PCRE_EXTENDED independent option bits from within the pattern. The content of the options argument specifies the initial setting at the start of compilation. You can set the PCRE_ANCHORED option at matching time and at compile time.

functions.name: pcreExecute
functions.syntax: pcreExecute(  o_comPatObj  S_subject  [ x_options ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Matches the subject string or symbol (S_subject) against a previously compiled pattern set up by the last pcreCompile call (o_comPatObj). The matching algorithm is PCRE/Perl-compatible. You can use a third (optional) argument to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern matching. You can use this function in conjunction with pcreCompile to match several subject strings or symbols against a single pattern.

functions.name: pcreGenCompileOptBits
functions.syntax: pcreGenCompileOptBits(  [ ?caseLess  g_setCaseLessp ] [ ?multiLine g_setMultiLinep ] [ ?dotAll    g_setDotAllp ] [ ?extended  g_setExtendedp ] [ ?anchored  g_setAnchoredp ] [ ?dollar_endonly g_setDollarEndonlyp ] [ ?ungreedy  g_setUngreedyp ] [ ?no_auto_capture g_setNoAutoCapturep ] [ ?firstline g_setFirstlinep ] )  => x_resultOptBits
functions.description: Generates bitwise inclusive OR-bor()-of zero or more independent option bits that affect compilation so that you can specify them symbolically in the pcreCompile function. If you call pcreGenCompileOptBits with no arguments, the function returns a zero (options have their default settings).

functions.name: pcreGenExecOptBits
functions.syntax: pcreGenExecOptBits(  [ ?anchored g_setAnchoredp ] [ ?notbol   g_setNotbolp ] [ ?noteol   g_setNoteolp ] [ ?notempty g_setNotemptyp ] [ ?partial  g_setPartialp ] ) => x_resultOptBits
functions.description: Generates bitwise inclusive OR-bor()-of zero or more independent option bits that affect pattern matching so that you can specify them symbolically in the pcreExecute function. If you call pcreGenExecOptBits with no arguments, the function returns a zero (options have their default settings).

functions.name: pcreGetRecursionLimit
functions.description: Returns the PCRE maximum recursion depth (stack depth) that is set by the pcreSetRecursionLimit() function. The default value is 10000000.

functions.name: pcreListCompileOptBits
functions.description: Displays information about the options used with pcreGenCompileOptBits. See the description of pcreGenCompileOptBits for more information.

functions.name: pcreListExecOptBits
functions.description: Displays information about the options used with pcreGenExecOptBits.

functions.name: pcreMatchAssocList
functions.syntax: pcreMatchAssocList(  g_pattern  l_subjects  [ x_compOptBits ]  [ x_execOptBits ] )  => l_results / nil / error message(s)
functions.description: Matches the keys of an association list of subjects (strings or symbols) against a regular expression pattern (g_pattern) and returns an association list of those elements that match. The keys are the first elements of each key/value pair in the association list. You can use optional arguments to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compiling and matching. The compiling and matching algorithms are PCRE/Perl-compatible.

functions.name: pcreMatchList
functions.syntax: pcreMatchList(  g_pattern  l_subjects  [ x_compOptBits ]  [ x_execOptBits ] )  => l_results / nil / error message(s)
functions.description: Matches a list of subjects (strings or symbols) against a regular expression pattern (g_pattern) and returns a list of those elements that match. You can use optional arguments to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compiling and matching. The compiling and matching algorithms are PCRE/Perl-compatible.

functions.name: pcreMatchp
functions.syntax: pcreMatchp(  g_pattern  S_subject  [ x_compOptBits ]  [ x_execOptBits ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Checks to see whether the subject string or symbol (S_subject) matches the specified regular expression pattern (g_pattern). You can use optional arguments to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compiling and matching. The compiling and matching algorithms are PCRE/Perl-compatible. For greater efficiency when matching a number of subjects against a single pattern, you should use pcreCompile and pcreExecute.

functions.name: pcreObjectp
functions.description: Checks to see whether the given argument is a pcreObject or not.

functions.name: pcrePrintLastMatchErr
functions.description: Prints the error message associated with the last failed matching operation (that is, when pcreExecute returns nil).

functions.name: pcreReplace
functions.syntax: pcreReplace(  o_comPatObj  t_source  t_replacement  x_index  [ x_options ] )  => t_result / t_source
functions.description: Replaces one or all occurrences of a previously-compiled regular expression in the given source string with the specified replacement string. The integer index indicates which of the matching substrings to replace. If the index is less than or equal to zero, the function applies the replacement string to all matching substrings. You can use an optional argument to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern matching. The matching algorithm is PCRE/Perl-compatible.

functions.name: pcreSetRecursionLimit
functions.description: Sets the maximum recursion depth for SKILL/PCRE match algorithms. The maximum recursion depth needs to be set for systems that have a low stack depth, in order to prevent crashes while using SKILL PCRE functions.

functions.name: pcreSubpatCount
functions.description: Counts the subpatterns in a PCRE pattern.

functions.name: pcreSubstitute
functions.description: If o_pcreObject is not provided, pcreSubstitute copies the input string and substitutes all pattern tags in it using the corresponding matched strings from the last pcreExecute/pcreMatch* operation.

functions.name: phoIPCGetMessageProcessor
functions.description: Returns the name of the message processor associated with the specified tool.

functions.name: phoIPCGetServerCheck
functions.description: Returns the name of the registered function that can be called to check if the server associated with the specified tool is operating correctly.

functions.name: phoIPCProcessMarkers
functions.syntax: phoIPCProcessMarkers( d_cellviewID l_markerList s_displayToolName ) => t / nil
functions.description: Specifies the default marker processor for the specified tool and generates markers in the Annotation Browser assistant, categorizing the markers based on the specified markerList.

functions.name: phoIPCProcessPorts
functions.syntax: phoIPCProcessPorts( d_cellviewID l_opticalPortList [ l_portMap ] [ l_lppMap ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Creates optical ports in the specified cellview using the specfied portList. This is the default optical port processor.

functions.name: phoIPCProcessServerMessage
functions.syntax: phoIPCProcessServerMessage( d_cellviewID t_waveguideLayer t_serverMessage [ g_dropPorts ] [ l_portMap ] [ l_lppMap ] )
functions.description: Issues messages from the IPC processor, which can further be used in Pcells to create geometries.

functions.name: phoIPCProcessShapes
functions.syntax: phoIPCProcessShapes( d_cellviewID l_shapeList l_portMap [ l_lppMap ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Uses shapeList to create shapes and electrical pins in the specified cellview. This is the default shape processor.

functions.name: phoIPCRegisterMessageProcessor
functions.description: Registers the message processor corresponding to the specified tool. In addition, the function ensures that the message processor function is defined and has the correct number of arguments.

functions.name: phoIPCRegisterServerCheck
functions.description: Registers a function that can be used to check if the server associated with the specified tool is operating correctly. The registered server check function is expected to have no arguments. If the function is not specified, or it has an argument, registration fails. If the function is registered, it checks that the IPC channel is open and connected to the child process. This function is intended to perform a quick check and is likely to be used inside a Pcell.

functions.name: phoIPCServerCheck
functions.description: Calls the registered server check function for the specified tool and issues a warning in the CIW if the server is not running. In addition, when a valid cellview is specified, the function creates a label at the origin that displays the same message in the layout canvas.

functions.name: plist
functions.description: Returns the property list associated with a symbol.

functions.name: plus
functions.description: Returns the result of adding one or more operands to the first operand. Prefix form of the + arithmetic operator.

functions.name: plusp
functions.description: Checks whether the given object is a positive number.

functions.name: popf
functions.description: A pop that uses the setf function. It returns the value for g_place that is removed.

functions.name: portp
functions.description: Checks if an object is an input or output port.

functions.name: postArrayDec
functions.description: Takes an array or an associated table element with an index g_index, decrements its value by one, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the original value. This function is a prefix form of s--.

functions.name: postArrayInc
functions.description: Takes an array or an associated table element with an index g_index, increments its value by one, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the original value. This function is a prefix form of s++.

functions.name: postArraySet
functions.description: Takes an array or an associated table element with an index g_index, adds an n_modifier value to its original value, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the original value.

functions.name: postdecrement
functions.description: Takes a variable, decrements its value by one, stores the new value back into the variable, and returns the original value. This function is a prefix form of s--. The name of the variable must be a symbol and the value must be a number.

functions.name: postincrement
functions.description: Takes a variable, increments its value by one, stores the new value back into the variable, and returns the original value. This function is a prefix form of s++. The name of the variable must be a symbol and the value must be a number.

functions.name: pp
functions.description: Pretty prints the definition of a function. The function must not be read-protected. This is an nlambda function.

functions.name: pprint
functions.description: Identical to print except that it pretty prints the value whenever possible.

functions.name: preArrayDec
functions.description: Takes an array or an associated table element with an index g_index, decrements its value by one, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the updated value. This function is a prefix form of --s.

functions.name: preArrayInc
functions.description: Takes an array or an associated table element with an index g_index, increments its value by one, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the updated value. This function is a prefix form of ++s.

functions.name: preArraySet
functions.description: Takes array or an associated table element with an index g_index, adds an n_modifier value to its original value, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the updated value.

functions.name: predecrement
functions.description: Takes a variable, decrements its value by one, stores the new value back into the variable, and returns the new value. This function is a prefix form of --s. The name of the variable must be a symbol and the value must be a number.

functions.name: preincrement
functions.description: Takes a variable, increments its value by one, stores the new value back into the variable, and returns the new value. This function is a prefix form of ++s. The name of the variable must be a symbol and the value must be a number.

functions.name: prependInstallPath
functions.description: Prepends the Cadence DFII installation path to a file or directory and returns the resulting path as a string.

functions.name: print
functions.description: Prints a SKILL object using the default format for the data type of the value.

functions.name: printFunctions
functions.description: Prints all function names that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression.

functions.name: printObject
functions.description: Writes a description of an object to an output port.

functions.name: printVariables
functions.description: Prints all variable names that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression, along with their values.

functions.name: printlev
functions.syntax: printlev(  g_value  x_level  x_length  [ p_outputPort ]  )  => nil
functions.description: Prints a list with a limited number of elements and levels of nesting.

functions.name: printself
functions.description: A generic function which is called to print a stdObject instance. You can define your own methods to this generic function for specializing on a class to alter the default print representation of an instance of that class.

functions.name: printstruct
functions.description: Prints the contents of an association table or defstruct in a tabular format.

functions.name: procedure
functions.description: Defines a function using a formal argument list. The body of the procedure is a list of expressions to evaluate.

functions.name: procedurep
functions.description: Checks if an object is a procedure, or function, object.

functions.name: profile
functions.description: Turns on global SKILL profiling for measuring time or memory.

functions.name: profileReset
functions.description: Resets all SKILL profiler data.

functions.name: profileSummary
functions.syntax: profileSummary(  [ ?file t_filename ]  [ ?sort s_sortKey ]  [ ?filters g_filterSpec ]  [ ?maxFns x_maxDisplayed ] [ ?minSecs f_minSecs ]  [ ?minBytes x_minBytes ] [ ?children g_showChildren ]  )  => t
functions.description: Prints a summary of profiling results, showing either the execution time or memory allocated to SKILL functions that were executed.

functions.name: prog
functions.syntax: prog(  l_localVariables  [  [ s_label ]  g_expr1  ] ...  ) => g_result / nil
functions.description: Allows for local variable bindings and permits abrupt exits on control jumps. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: prog1
functions.description: Evaluates expressions from left to right and returns the value of the first expression. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: prog2
functions.description: Evaluates expressions from left to right and returns the value of the second expression. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: progn
functions.description: Evaluates expressions from left to right and returns the value of the last expression. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: pushf
functions.description: A push that uses the setf function. It modifies the contents of the original storage location.

functions.name: putc
functions.description: Puts the x_symbol to p_port (to complement getc function)

functions.name: putd
functions.description: Assigns a new function binding, which must be a function, a lambda expression, or nil, to a function name. If you just want to define a function, use procedure or defun.

functions.name: putprop
functions.description: Adds properties to symbols or disembodied property lists.

functions.name: putpropq
functions.syntax: putpropq(  sl_id  g_value  S_name  )  => g_value  sl_id->S_name = g_value  => g_value
functions.description: Adds properties to symbols or disembodied property lists. Identical to putprop except that S_name is not evaluated. If the property already exists, the old value is replaced with a new one.

functions.name: putpropqq
functions.syntax: putpropqq(  s_id  g_value  S_name  )  => g_value  s_id.S_name = g_value  => g_value
functions.description: Adds properties to symbols. Identical to putprop except that sl_id and S_name are not evaluated. If the property already exists, the old value is replaced with a new one.

functions.name: quote
functions.description: Returns the name of the variable or the expression. This function is a prefix form of the ' operator. Quoting is used to prevent expressions from being evaluated.

functions.name: quotient
functions.description: Returns the result of dividing the first operand by one or more operands. Prefix form of the / arithmetic operator.

functions.name: range
functions.description: Returns a list whose first element is n_num1 and whose tail is n_num2. This function is a prefix form of the : operator.

functions.name: read
functions.description: Parses and returns the next expression from an input port.

functions.name: readTable
functions.description: Reads and appends the contents of a file to an existing association table.

functions.name: readstring
functions.description: Returns the first expression in a string. Subsequent expressions in the string are ignored. The expression is not processed in any way.

functions.name: realp
functions.description: Checks whether the specified value is a real number. Same as floatp.

functions.name: regExitAfter
functions.description: Registers the action to be taken after the exit function has performed its bookkeeping tasks but before it returns control to the operating system.

functions.name: regExitBefore
functions.description: Registers the action to be taken before the exit function is executed. If the function registered returns the ignoreExit symbol, the exit is aborted.

functions.name: remExitProc
functions.description: Removes a registered exit procedure.

functions.name: remainder
functions.description: Returns the remainder of dividing two integers. The remainder is either zero or has the sign of the dividend. Same as mod.

functions.name: remd
functions.description: Removes all top-level elements equal to a SKILL object from a list. This is a destructive removal, which means that the original list itself is modified. Therefore, any other reference to that list will also see the changes.

functions.name: remdq
functions.description: Removes all top-level elements that are identical to a SKILL object using eq from a list. This is a destructive removal, which means that the original list itself is modified. Therefore, any other reference to that list will also see the changes.

functions.name: remove
functions.syntax: remove(  g_x  l_arg  )  => l_result  remove(  g_key  o_table  )  => g_value
functions.description: Returns a copy of a list with all top-level elements equal to a SKILL object removed. Can also be used to remove an entry from an association table, in which case the removal is destructive, that is, any other reference to the table will also see the changes. remove uses equal for comparison. remove can also be used with an association table to identify and remove an entry corresponding to the key specified in the function.

functions.name: removeDependent
functions.description: Removes a dependent object from the given object.

functions.name: removeFromExportList
functions.description: Removes symbols referenced in l_symbolList from the export list of its namespace. This function will not throw an error, if some of the symbols are not exported. If a symbol from l_symbolList was imported by useNamespace it will not removed by unuseNamespace.

functions.name: removeListDuplicates
functions.description: Removes duplicate entries from a SKILL list and returns a new list with the duplicates removed.

functions.name: removeMethod
functions.syntax: removeMethod(  s_genFunction  g_className  [ g_method ] )  => t / nil
functions.description: Removes a given method from a generic function.

functions.name: removeShadowImport
functions.description: Removes the specified symbols from the namespace shadow list.

functions.name: remprop
functions.description: Removes a property from a property list and returns the property's former value.

functions.name: remq
functions.description: Returns a copy of a list with all top-level elements that are identical to a SKILL object removed. Uses eq.

functions.name: renameFile
functions.description: The renameFile() function changes the name of a file or directory.The S_old argument points to the pathname of the file or directory to be renamed. The S_new argument points to the new pathname of the file or directory. If the SKILL path is nil, renameFile() would search the current directory. Otherwise, the SKILL path would be searched first for S_old. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

functions.name: restoreFloat
functions.description: Restores a floating point number (f_number) from its serialized string (t_string) representation. t_string should be created by saveFloat().

functions.name: resume
functions.description: Exits the interactive top-level loop started with the most recently invoked toplevel function and returns its argument to the caller of toplevel. Do not use this function programmatically; use it only as an interactive command.

functions.name: return
functions.description: Forces the enclosing prog to exit and returns the given value. The return statement has meaning only when used inside a prog statement.

functions.name: reverse
functions.description: Returns a copy of the given list with the elements in reverse order.

functions.name: rexCompile
functions.description: Compiles a regular expression string pattern into an internal representation to be used by succeeding calls to rexExecute.

functions.name: rexExecute
functions.description: Matches a string or symbol against the previously compiled pattern set up by the last rexCompile call.

functions.name: rexMagic
functions.description: Turns on or off the special interpretation associated with the meta-characters in regular expressions.

functions.name: rexMatchAssocList
functions.description: Returns a new association list created out of those elements of the given association list whose key matches a regular expression pattern. The supplied regular expression pattern overwrites the previously compiled pattern and is used for subsequent matching until the next new pattern is provided.

functions.name: rexMatchList
functions.description: Creates a new list of those strings or symbols in the given list that match a regular expression pattern. The supplied regular expression pattern overwrites the previously compiled pattern and is used for subsequent matching until the next new pattern is provided.

functions.name: rexMatchp
functions.description: Checks to see if a string or symbol matches a given regular expression pattern. The supplied regular expression pattern overwrites the previously compiled pattern and is used for subsequent matching until the next new pattern is provided.

functions.name: rexReplace
functions.description: Returns a copy of the source string in which the specified substring instances that match the last compiled regular expression are replaced with the given string.

functions.name: rexSubstitute
functions.description: Substitutes the pattern tags in the argument string with previously matched (sub)strings.

functions.name: rightshift
functions.description: Returns the integer result of shifting a value a specified number of bits to the right. Prefix form of the >> arithmetic operator. rightshift is logical (that is, vacated bits are 0-filled).

functions.name: rindex
functions.description: Returns a string consisting of the remainder of string1 beginning with the last occurrence of string2.

functions.name: rotatef
functions.description: Modifies the value of each place by rotating the values from one place to another in a cyclic order.

functions.name: round2
functions.description: This function is a version of the round function that rounds the result in floating-point calculations to its closest integer value.

functions.name: rplaca
functions.description: Replaces the first element of a list with an object. This function does not create a new list; it alters the input list, in the same way as setcar. This is a destructive operation, meaning that any other reference to the list will also see the change.

functions.name: rplacd
functions.description: Replaces the tail of a list with the elements of a second list. This function does not create a new list; it alters the input list in the same way as setcdr. This is a destructive operation, meaning that any other reference to the list will also see the changes.

functions.name: saveContext
functions.description: Saves the current state of the SKILL language interpreter as a binary file. This function must be used in conjunction with setContext.

functions.name: saveFloat
functions.description: Serializes the given floating point number (f_number) to string (t_string).

functions.name: schemeTopLevelEnv
functions.description: Returns the top level SKILL++ environment as an environment object.

functions.name: set
functions.description: Sets a variable to a new value. Similar to setq but the first argument for set is evaluated.

functions.name: setContext
functions.description: Allows contexts to be saved incrementally, creating micro contexts from a session's SKILL context.

functions.name: setFnWriteProtect
functions.description: Prevents a named function from being redefined.

functions.name: setPrompts
functions.description: Sets the prompt text string for the CIW. The first prompt is used to indicate the topmost top-level. The second prompt is used whenever a nested top-level is entered.

functions.name: setSG
functions.description: Evaluates and then sets the value for the specified attribute or property. It is a lambda implementation of setSGq().

functions.name: setSaveContextVersion
functions.description: Resets the current saveContext version to x_newVers and returns the previous context version. If x_newVers has an unsupported value or the function is called between setContext and saveContext, it returns an error.

functions.name: setShellEnvVar
functions.description: Sets or updates the value of the UNIX environment variable. This function expands the environment variable name specified in the argument.

functions.name: setSkillPath
functions.description: Sets the internal SKILL path used by some file-related functions in resolving relative path names.

functions.name: setSlotValue
functions.description: Sets the s_slotName slot of g_standardObject to g_value.

functions.name: setVarWriteProtect
functions.description: (SKILL mode only) Sets the write-protection on a variable to prevent its value from being updated. Does not work in SKILL++ mode.

functions.name: setarray
functions.syntax: setarray(  a_array  x_index  g_value  )  => g_value  setarray(  o_table  g_key  g_value  )  => g_value
functions.description: Assigns the given value to the specified element of an array or to the specified key of a table. Normally this function is invoked implicitly using the array-subscription syntax, such as, x[i] = v.

functions.name: setcar
functions.description: Replaces the first element of a list with an object in the same way as rplaca. This is a destructive operation, meaning that any other reference to the list will also see the change.

functions.name: setcdr
functions.description: Replaces the tail of a list with the elements of a second list in the same way as rplacd. This is a destructive operation, meaning that any other reference to the list will also see the change.

functions.name: setf
functions.syntax: setf(  g_place  g_value  )  => g_result  setf(  g_place := g_value => g_result
functions.description: Assigns a new value to an existing storage location, destroying the value that was previously in that location. setf is the same as the assignment (:=) operator. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: setf_<helper>
functions.description: An expander function for setf, which returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with the expander name.

functions.name: setf_arrayref
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with arrayref.

functions.name: setf_bottomEdge
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with bottomEdge.

functions.name: setf_caaar
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with caar.

functions.name: setf_caadr
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with caadr.

functions.name: setf_caar
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with caar.

functions.name: setf_cadar
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cadar.

functions.name: setf_caddr
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with caddr.

functions.name: setf_cadr
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cadr.

functions.name: setf_car
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with car.

functions.name: setf_cdaar
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cdaar.

functions.name: setf_cdadr
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cdadr.

functions.name: setf_cdar
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cdar.

functions.name: setf_cddar
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cddar.

functions.name: setf_cdddr
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cdddr.

functions.name: setf_cddr
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cddr.

functions.name: setf_cdr
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cdr.

functions.name: setf_dynamic
functions.description: Evaluates g_value in the current lexical scope and updates the SKILL variable named s_name.

functions.name: setf_get
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with get.

functions.name: setf_getSG
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getSG.

functions.name: setf_getSGq
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getSGq.

functions.name: setf_getShellEnvVar
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getShellEnvVar.

functions.name: setf_getd
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getd.

functions.name: setf_getq
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getq.

functions.name: setf_getqq
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getqq.

functions.name: setf_last
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with last.

functions.name: setf_leftEdge
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with leftEdge.

functions.name: setf_lowerLeft
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with lowerLeft.

functions.name: setf_nth
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation to support setf(nth(...) ...) expressions. In the function, replace helper with nth.

functions.name: setf_nthcdr
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with nthedr.

functions.name: setf_nthedr
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with nthcdr.

functions.name: setf_nthelem
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with nthelem.

functions.name: setf_rightEdge
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with rightEdge.

functions.name: setf_slotValue
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with slotValue.

functions.name: setf_topEdge
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with topEdge.

functions.name: setf_upperRight
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with upperRight.

functions.name: setf_xCoord
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with xCoord.

functions.name: setf_yCoord
functions.description: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with yCoord.

functions.name: setguard
functions.description: Mainly enforces disciplined use of a symbol as a global variable by associating it with a guarding function that is either a symbol that identifies the name of the guarding function or a lambda form (just like the first argument to the apply function). If the guarding function is nil, the symbol is unguarded. The guarding function is called with two arguments whenever a new value is assigned to the symbol: the symbol and the value to be assigned to it. The result of the guarding function determines the setguard return value that gets assigned to the symbol.

functions.name: setof
functions.description: Returns a new list containing only those elements in a list or the keys in an association table that satisfy an expression. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: setofs
functions.description: Returns a new list containing only those elements in a list or the keys in an association table that satisfy an expression. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable (s_formalVar) in a let block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart setof. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: setplist
functions.description: Sets the property list of an object to a new property list; the old property list attached to the object is lost.

functions.name: setq
functions.syntax: setq(  s_variableName  g_newValueExp  )  => g_result  setq(  s_variableName = g_newValue  )  => g_result
functions.description: Sets a variable to a new value. setq is the same as the assignment (=) operator. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: setqbitfield
functions.syntax: setqbitfield(  s_var  x_val  x_msb  x_lsb  )  => x_result
functions.description: Sets a value into a set of bits in the bit field specified by the variable s_var, stores the new value back into the variable, and then returns the new value. Prefix form of the <:>= operator.

functions.name: setqbitfield1
functions.description: Sets a value into a single bit in the bit field specified by the variable s_var, stores the new value back into the variable, and then returns the new value. Prefix form of the <>= operator.

functions.name: sh, shell
functions.syntax: sh(  [ t_command ]  )  => t / nil   shell(  [ t_command ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Starts the UNIX Bourne shell sh as a child process to execute a command string.

functions.name: shadow
functions.description: Adds symbols s_symbol to the shadow list of the default namespace. The symbols which are added to the shadow list are not overridden by import.

functions.name: shadowImport
functions.description: Adds symbols to the namespace shadow list. By default, all warnings related to namespaces are suppressed in the shadowImport function.

functions.name: sharedInitialize
functions.syntax: sharedInitialize(  g_object  g_slotList  @rest l_initargs  ) => g_object / error
functions.description: This is a generic function, which is called when an instance is created, re-initialized, updated to conform to a redefined class, or updated to conform to a different class. It is called from the initializeInstance, updateInstanceForRedefinedClass, and updateInstanceForDifferentClass functions to initialize slots of the instance g_object using the corresponding initforms.

functions.name: simplifyFilename
functions.description: Expands the name of a file to its full path.

functions.name: simplifyFilenameUnique
functions.description: Returns the full path for the given t_path without links and a trailing slash / at the end of the result string. The function returns an error if the given t_path is incorrect.

functions.name: skDisableMessage
functions.description: Disables a SKILL Lint message from being reported inside a given function definition.

functions.name: skDisableMessageBlock
functions.description: Disables one or a list of SKILL Lint messages from being reported by rules within the body of the function. You might want to turn off certain rules temporarily, and not globally, inside a particular block of code. SKILL Lint will recognize a call to this function if inserted inside the block of code being analyzed.

functions.name: skEnableMessageBlock
functions.description: Re-enables reporting of one or more SKILL Lint messages that have been globally turned off within the body of this function only.

functions.name: skIgnoreMessage
functions.description: Turns off the reporting of specified SKILL Lint messages. For a message to appear, both the message and its group have to be unignored.

functions.name: skTabulate
functions.syntax: skTabulate(  ?fileNames g_tabulatedFileNames [ ?reportFile t_reportFile ]  [ ?showFile g_showFile ]  [ ?dontResolveSymLink g_dontResolveSymLink ]  [ ?customerInfo l_customerInfo ]  [ ?printFiltered g_printFiltered ]  [ ?ext l_ext ]  [ ?infoFile g_infoFile ]  [ ?defnFile g_defnFile ]  [ ?recurse g_recurse ]  [ ?exclude g_exclude ]  [ ?recurseExclude g_recurseExclude ]  [ ?sendReport g_sendReport ]  => t
functions.description: Runs the SKILL Tabulator in batch mode.

functions.name: skTabulateSKILL
functions.description: Brings up the SKILL Tabulator UI form.

functions.name: skUnignoreMessage
functions.description: Turns on the reporting of specified SKILL Lint messages. For a message to appear, both the message and its group have to be unignored.

functions.name: skillDebugger
functions.description: Activates the SKILL Debugger. Usually invoked by a break or error handler.

functions.name: skillDevStatus
functions.description: Returns the current status of the Cadence SKILL Development Environment license.

functions.name: sklint
functions.syntax: sklint( [ ?file tl_inputFileName ] [ ?context t_contextName ] [ ?outputFile t_outputFileName ] [ ?ignoreGroups l_ignoreGroups ] [ ?globals l_globals ] [ ?depends l_depends ] [ ?rulesFile t_rulesFile ] [ ?ignores l_ignoresMessageList ] [ ?checkNlambda g_checkNlambda ] [ ?noPrintLog g_noPrintLog ] [ ?useGlobalIgnores g_useGlobalIgnores ] [ ?useGlobalRulesFileList g_useGlobalRulesFileList ] [ ?useDisableMessages g_useDisableMessages ] [ ?checkCdsFuncs g_checkCdsFuncs ] [ ?checkPvtFuncs g_checkPvtFuncs ] [ ?checkPubFuncs g_checkPubFuncs ] [ ?prefixes l_prefixList ] [ ?checkCdsPrefixes g_checkCdsPrefixes ] [ ?checkFuncPrefixes g_checkFuncPrefixes ] [ ?tabulate g_tabulate ] [ ?skPath t_skPath ] [ ?codeVersion t_release ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Checks a SKILL file or context and reports potential errors and ways to clean up your code.

functions.name: slotBoundp
functions.description: Checks if a named slot is bound to an instance or not.

functions.name: slotUnbound
functions.description: This function is called when the slotValue function attempts to reference an unbound slot. It signals that the value of the slot s_slotName of g_object has not been set yet. In this case, slotValue returns the result of the method.

functions.name: slotValue
functions.description: Returns the value contained in the slot slotName of the given standardObject.

functions.name: sort
functions.description: Sorts a list according to the specified comparison function. By default, the sort function uses alphalessp, which defaults to an alphabetical sort when u_comparefn is nil. This function does not create a new list. It returns the altered input list. This is a destructive operation. The l_data list is modified in place and no new storage is allocated. Pointers previously pointing to l_data may not be pointing at the head of the sorted list.

functions.name: sortcar
functions.description: Similar to sort except that only the car of each element in a list is used for comparison by the sort function. This function does not create a new list. It returns the altered input list.

functions.name: sprintf
functions.description: Formats the output and assigns the resultant string to the variable given as the first argument.

functions.name: sstatus
functions.description: Sets the internal system variable named to a given value. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: stacktrace
functions.syntax: stacktrace(  [ g_unevaluated ]  [ x_depth ]  [ x_skip ]  [ p_port ]  )  => x_result
functions.description: Prints the functions on the stack and their arguments to the depth specified, or to the bottom of the stack if no depth is specified.

functions.name: startFinder
functions.description: Starts the SKILL API Finder utility. If the t_funcName argument is provided, the corresponding documentation of the function is displayed in the Finder. If a Finder window is already open, it will be updated or a new window will be displayed. The Finder window remains open, unless specifically closed, even after the parent window has been closed.

functions.name: status
functions.description: Returns the value of the internal system variable named. This nlambda function also works in SKILL++ mode.

functions.name: step
functions.description: Steps into functions and executes a given number of SKILL functions. This function only works if executed from within a break handler and if the code you want to step through was loaded under debugMode. See installDebugger.

functions.name: stepend
functions.description: Allows execution to proceed to the end of the nth enclosing form and displays its result. stepend cannot proceed past the end of the current function. This function only works if executed from within a break handler and if the code you want to step through was loaded under debugMode. See installDebugger.

functions.name: stepout
functions.description: Allows execution to proceed until the evaluator returns from the current function.

functions.name: strcat
functions.description: Takes input strings or symbols and concatenates them.

functions.name: strcmp
functions.description: Compares two argument strings alphabetically.

functions.name: stringToFunction
functions.description: Wraps and converts a string of SKILL code into a parameterless SKILL function.

functions.name: stringToSymbol
functions.description: Converts a string to a symbol of the same name.

functions.name: stringToTime
functions.description: Given a date and time string, returns an integer time value representation. The time argument must be in the format as returned by the timeToString function, such as: June 28 16:57:06 2022.

functions.name: stringp
functions.description: Checks if an object is a string.

functions.name: strlen
functions.description: Returns the number of characters in a string.

functions.name: strncat
functions.description: Creates a new string by appending a maximum number of characters from t_string2 to t_string1.

functions.name: strncmp
functions.description: Compares two argument strings alphabetically only up to a maximum number of characters.

functions.name: strpbrk
functions.description: Returns a substring of the first occurence in t_str1 of any character from the string pointed to by t_str2

functions.name: subclassesOf
functions.description: Returns the ordered list of all (immediate) subclasses of u_classObject. Each element in the list is a class object.

functions.name: subclassp
functions.description: Predicate function that checks if classObject1 is a subclass of classObject2.

functions.name: subst
functions.description: Substitutes one object for another object in a list.

functions.name: substring
functions.syntax: substring(  S_string  x_index  [ x_length ]  )  => t_result / nil
functions.description: Creates a new substring from an input string, starting at an index point and continuing for a given length.

functions.name: superclassesOf
functions.description: Returns the ordered list of all super classes of u_classObject. Each element in the list is a class object.

functions.name: sxtd
functions.description: Sign-extends the number represented by the rightmost specified number of bits in the given integer.

functions.name: symbolToString
functions.description: Converts a symbol to a string of the same name. This function is the same as get_pname.

functions.name: symbolp
functions.description: Checks if an object is a symbol.

functions.name: symeval
functions.description: Returns the value of the named variable.

functions.name: symstrp
functions.description: Checks if an object is either a symbol or a string.

functions.name: system
functions.description: Spawns a separate UNIX process to execute a command.

functions.name: tableToList
functions.description: Converts the contents of an association table to an association list. Use this function interactively to look at the contents of a table.

functions.name: tablep
functions.description: Checks if an object is an association table.

functions.name: tailp
functions.description: Returns arg1 if a list cell eq to arg1 is found by cdr down arg2 zero or more times. It returns nil otherwise. Because eq is being used for comparison l_arg1 must point to a tail list in l_arg2 for this predicate to return a non-nil value.

functions.name: tconc
functions.description: Creates a list cell whose car points to a list of the elements being constructed and whose cdr points to the last list cell of the list being constructed.

functions.name: theEnvironment
functions.description: (SKILL++ mode only) Returns the top level environment if called from a SKILL++ top-level. Returns the enclosing lexical environment if called within a SKILL++ function. Returns the associated environment if passed a SKILL++ function object. Otherwise returns nil.

functions.name: throw
functions.description: Transfers the control back to the return point established in a catch block. The argument value is used as the value to be passed. The throw function should always be used inside catch(. . . g_form . . .).

functions.name: timeToString
functions.description: Takes an integer UNIX time value, returns a formatted string that the value denotes. The string is always in a form like: Dec 28 16:57:06 2021.

functions.name: timeToTm
functions.description: Given an integer time value, returns a tm structure.

functions.name: times
functions.description: Returns the result of multiplying the first operand by one or more operands. Prefix form of the * arithmetic operator.

functions.name: tmToTime
functions.description: Given a tm structure, returns the integer value of the time it represents.

functions.name: toplevel
functions.description: Starts an interactive top-level loop in either SKILL or SKILL++ mode.

functions.name: tracef
functions.description: Turns on tracing of specified functions. Shows the functions called with their evaluated arguments and return values. This is an nlambda function.

functions.name: tracelevlimit
functions.description: Limits the indentation level and hence the call depth while tracing functions, arrays, or variables.

functions.name: tracelevunlimit
functions.description: Turns off limiting of the indentation level and hence the call depth while tracing functions, arrays, or variables.

functions.name: tracep
functions.description: Turns on tracing of assignments to specified properties. This is an nlambda function.

functions.name: tracev
functions.description: Turns on tracing of assignments to specified variables. This is an nlambda function.

functions.name: truename
functions.description: Tries to find the specified file (t_string) and returns the full path to the file.

functions.name: truncate
functions.description: Truncates a given number to an integer.

functions.name: type, typep
functions.syntax: type(  s_object  )  => s_type   typep(  s_object  )  => s_type
functions.description: Returns a symbol that indicates the type of a SKILL object. The functions type and typep are identical. The suffix p is usually added to the name of a function to indicate that it is a predicate function.

functions.name: unalias
functions.description: Undefines the aliases specified in an argument list and returns a list containing the aliases undefined by the call. This is nlambda function also works in SKILL++ mode.

functions.name: unbindVar
functions.description: Resets a SKILL or Scheme variable so that its value becomes unbound.

functions.name: unbreakpt
functions.description: Clears breakpoints. This is an nlambda function.

functions.name: unbreakptMethod
functions.description: Removes breakpoints set on the specified method.

functions.name: uncount
functions.description: Turns off counting and returns the current count results. This is an nlambda function.

functions.name: unimportSymbol
functions.description: Unimports symbols from the given namespace. By default, this function unimports from the IL (or default) namespace.

functions.name: uninstallDebugger
functions.description: Uninstalls the SKILL debugger as the error handler. Turns off debug mode.

functions.name: unprofile
functions.description: Turns off SKILL profiling but does not reset.

functions.name: unsetShellEnvVar
functions.description: Removes an environment variable from the environment of the calling process. This function expands the environment variable name specified in the argument. If the environment variable (t_envVarName) does not exist in the current environment, the environment is left unchanged.

functions.name: untrace
functions.description: Turns tracing off for all functions specified that were traced using the tracef function. This is an nlambda function.

functions.name: untracep
functions.description: Turns off tracing of the specified properties. This is an nlambda function.

functions.name: untracev
functions.description: Turns off tracing for assignments to specified variables. This is an nlambda function.

functions.name: unuseNamespace
functions.description: Unsets the specified namespace.

functions.name: unwatch
functions.description: Clears watchpoints set on the specified variables.

functions.name: unwindProtect
functions.description: Evaluates the g_protectedForm expression and then executes the SKILL g_cleanupForm expression. Even if the evaluation of g_protectedForm is interrupted or encounters an error, the g_cleanupForm expression is still executed. You can therefore use g_cleanupForm to close open file handles, reset variables, and restore the state to a known value.

functions.name: updateDependent
functions.syntax: updateDependent( u_class g_dependent s_notifType u_classObj ) => t
functions.description: Updates the dependents of a SKILL object, which could be a class or a generic function, when the SKILL object is modified. The SKILL engine calls this method for each g_dependent at different times. For example, if g_dependent is a method, the SKILL engine calls updateDependent at the time of adding or removing the method; whereas, for dependent classes the SKILL engine calls the updateDependent method at the end of class creation.

functions.name: updateInstanceForDifferentClass
functions.description: A generic function, which is called from changeClass to update the specified instance (g_currentObj).

functions.name: updateInstanceForRedefinedClass
functions.syntax: updateInstanceForRedefinedClass(  g_obj  l_addedSlots  l_deletedSlots  l_dplList  )  => t
functions.description: A generic function, which is called to update all instances of a class, when a class redefinition occurs.

functions.name: upperCase
functions.description: Returns a string that is a copy of the given argument with the lowercase alphabetic characters replaced by their uppercase equivalents.

functions.name: useNamespace
functions.description: Sets the given namespace for use and imports its symbols into the current namespace.

functions.name: vector
functions.description: Returns a vector or array, filled with the arguments in the given order. The vector function is analogous to the list function.

functions.name: vectorToList
functions.description: Returns a list containing the elements of an array.

functions.name: vectorp
functions.description: Checks whether the specified object is a vector. The behavior of this SKILL function is the same as arrayp.

functions.name: vi, vii, vil
functions.syntax: vi(  [ S_fileName ]  )  => t / nil  vii [ S_fileName ]  )  => t / nil viii [ S_fileName ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Edits a file using the vi editor. This is an nlambda function. Edits the named file using the vi editor, and optionally includes (vii) or loads (vil) the file into SKILL after exiting the editor. These functions are just variants of ed, edi, and edl with explicit request for using the vi editor.

functions.name: warn
functions.description: Buffers a warning message with given arguments inserted using the same format specification as sprintf, printf, and fprintf.

functions.name: watch
functions.description: Sets watchpoints on the specified variables. If watch() is called without arguments, it returns the list of variables being watched. If no variables are being watched, it returns nil.

functions.name: where
functions.syntax: where(  [ g_unevaluated ]  [ x_depth ]  [ x_skip ]  [ p_port ]  )  => x_result
functions.description: Prints the functions on the stack and their arguments to the depth specified, or to the bottom of the stack, including the local variables and their bindings.

functions.name: whereIs
functions.description: Prints the last file loaded in debug mode in which a function was defined, as well as the starting line number.

functions.name: which
functions.description: Returns the absolute path of the given context file, or regular file or directory.

functions.name: write
functions.description: Prints a SKILL object using the default format for the data type of the value.

functions.name: writeTable
functions.description: Writes the contents of an association table to a file with one key/value pair per line.

functions.name: xCoord
functions.description: Returns the first element of a list. Does not modify the argument list.

functions.name: xcons
functions.description: Adds an element to the beginning of a list. Equivalent to cons but the order of the arguments is reversed.

functions.name: xdifference
functions.description: Returns the integer result of subtracting one or more operands from the first operand. xdifference is an integer-only arithmetic function while difference can handle integers and floating-point numbers. xdifference runs slightly faster than difference in integer arithmetic calculation.

functions.name: xplus
functions.description: Returns the integer result of adding one or more operands to the first operand. xplus is an integer-only arithmetic function while plus can handle integers and floating-point numbers. xplus runs slightly faster than plus in integer arithmetic calculation.

functions.name: xquotient
functions.description: Returns the integer result of dividing the first operand by one or more operands. xquotient is an integer-only arithmetic function while quotient can handle integers and floating-point numbers. xquotient runs slightly faster than quotient in integer arithmetic calculation.

functions.name: xtimes
functions.description: Returns the integer result of multiplying the first operand by one or more operands. xtimes is an integer-only arithmetic function while times can handle integers and floating-point numbers. xtimes runs slightly faster than times in integer arithmetic calculation.

functions.name: yCoord
functions.description: Returns the tail of the list, that is, the list without its first element.

functions.name: zerop
functions.description: Checks whether the specified object is equal to zero. zerop is a predicate function.

functions.name: zxtd
functions.description: Zero-extends the number represented by the rightmost specified number of bits in the given integer.

functions.name: ciAPRCascodeIterator
functions.description: Iterator for advanced place and route cascoded structures.

functions.name: ciAPRDIDeviceGroupIterator
functions.description: Runs an iterator to identify advanced place and route Design Intent structures in the specified design.

functions.name: ciAPRDINetIterator
functions.description: Iterates through all nets that are associated with an APR Net Design Intent in the cellview. The iterator expression is the APR Net DI profile name, for example, APR Net Shielding.

functions.name: ciAPRXYInstSymmetricIterator
functions.syntax: ciAPRXYInstSymmetricIterator(  d_cellview t_finderExpr [ ?trigger g_trigger ] [ ?likeSchemaSym g_likeSchemaSym ] ) => list / nil
functions.description: Evaluates the finderExpr with the current symmetric pair of objects with common source or drain terminal names that are assigned to L and R local variables. This iterator is customized for the Auto-Device Placement and Routing flow and is used by the Circuit Prospector ADA finders to iterate over all symmetric design instance pairs with common source or drain terminal names, collecting them into symmetric pairs if the result of evaluating the passed expression (finderExpr) is not nil.

functions.name: ciActiveSameCellAndSizeIterator
functions.description: Returns a list of devices where each sub-list corresponds to two or more active devices that have the same cell and size in the cellview. If the finder match net expression evaluates to nil, the device is ignored.

functions.name: ciAddHierarchicalNotes
functions.syntax: ciAddHierarchicalNotes(  t_libName t_cellName t_viewName [ g_hierarchical ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Adds notes to the templates and constraints for a single cellview or all along the hierarchy beginning from the given cellview.

functions.name: ciAddLeadingSlash
functions.description: Adds a forward slash (/) to the beginning of the passed string if it does not already have one.

functions.name: ciAddProcessRules
functions.syntax: ciAddProcessRules(  d_Id l_rules [ t_parameterType ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Adds the specified process rules to the front of the rules associated with the given object.

functions.name: ciAddRuleGroup
functions.syntax: ciAddRuleGroup(  [ d_techID | d_cellViewID ] t_name ) => t / nil
functions.description: Creates an oaConstraint group, with a given name, for technology or design files.

functions.name: ciAddStructArg
functions.syntax: ciAddStructArg(  s_structType l_newArg [ ?afterArgName g_afterArgName ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Adds a new constraint generator argument to the list of existing arguments registered for the passed structType. By default, the argument is appended to the current list of arguments for the structType. Optionally, the new argument can be inserted after the end of the argument or after a existing argument name.

functions.name: ciAddTrailingSlash
functions.description: Adds a forward slash (/) to the end of the passed string if it does not already have one.

functions.name: ciAlignPinsOnCellSide
functions.syntax: ciAlignPinsOnCellSide(  u_cache l_memberList [ ?side t_side ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Generates alignment constraints for pins on the same side.

functions.name: ciAllCellViewsInHierarchy
functions.syntax: ciAllCellViewsInHierarchy(  d_cellViewDBId [ t_pathToCurrentCellView ] [ t_pathFilter ] [ t_depth ] [ s_predicate ] ) => list / nil
functions.description: Returns a list of disembodied property lists containing the path and database ID of each cellview in the hierarchy, or to a specific depth starting from a given cellview and path to that cellview.

functions.name: ciAxisCreate
functions.syntax: ciAxisCreate(  u_cache t_axisName [ l_parameterList ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Creates a new axis.

functions.name: ciAxisDelete
functions.syntax: ciAxisDelete(  u_cache t_axisName [ g_forceDelete ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Deletes an axis from the specified cache.

functions.name: ciAxisExists
functions.description: Returns t (true) if the named axis exists in the cache. Access to axes is only provided through the axis name. No direct reference to an axis object is provided.

functions.name: ciAxisListCon
functions.description: Lists all the constraints that are attached to a given axis.

functions.name: ciAxisListParams
functions.syntax: ciAxisListParams(  u_cache t_axisName [ g_includeDefaults ] ) => parameterList / nil
functions.description: Lists the parameters associated with an axis.

functions.name: ciAxisReplaceParams
functions.syntax: ciAxisReplaceParams(  u_cache t_axisName l_parameterList ) => t / nil
functions.description: Replaces all axis constraint parameters with a new set of parameters.

functions.name: ciBasicGetParamValue
functions.description: This API is similar to ciGetParamValue, except it does not evaluate iPar or pPar expressions. It gets the parameter value of the user defined parameter. The user-defined parameter was mapped to its PDK names by the ciMapParam function.

functions.name: ciBlockResistorArrayIterator
functions.description: Iterates over all resistor devices in the cellview based on the result of evaluating the passed or matched expression. This function is used by the Block Resistor Array finder of the Circuit Prospector assistant.

functions.name: ciBuildModgenParams
functions.syntax: ciBuildModgenParams(  g_cache l_devInfo l_pattern r_nil l_args ) => l_modgenParamsAndMembers
functions.description: Creates modgen parameter and member list. This is a utility function.

functions.name: ciBundleSignalsIterator
functions.description: Used by the Circuit Prospector assistant to iterate over all named bundle and bus nets. It returns the list of corresponding signals. The signals are grouped according to the result of the match expression. If the match expression evaluates to nil the signal list is ignored.

functions.name: ciCPRegistrationFromLAM
