functions.description: Creates a list containing the elements of l_list1 followed by the elements of l_list2 or returns the original association table including new entries.

functions.name: append1
functions.description: Adds new arguments to the end of a list.

functions.name: apply
functions.description: Applies the given function to the given argument list.

functions.name: argc
functions.description: Returns the number of arguments passed to a SKILL script. Used to enhance the SKILL script environment. This function works only for scripting with SKILL standalone executable (skill).

functions.name: arglist
functions.description: Returns the number and types of arguments expected for a function. Also checks if the specified function is a binary object,

functions.name: argv
functions.description: Returns the arguments passed to a SKILL script. Used to enhance the SKILL script environment. This function works only for scripting with SKILL standalone executable (skill).

functions.name: arrayp
functions.description: Checks if an object is an array.

functions.name: arrayref
functions.description: Returns the element in a collection that is in an array or a table of the given index.

functions.name: assert
functions.description: Enables you to insert assertions into the SKILL code, either at the top-level or within a function. It evaluates the expression (g_expression) and returns nil if the expression value is non-nil. Otherwise, throws an error and returns the unevaluated expression.

functions.name: assoc, assv, assq
functions.description: The assoc, assq, and assv functions find the first list in l_alist whose car field is g_key and return that list. assq uses eq to compare g_key with the car fields of the lists in alist. assoc uses equal. assv uses eqv.

functions.name: atan2
functions.description: Computes the principal value of the arc tangent of n_y/n_x, using the signs of both arguments to determine the quadrant of the return value.

functions.name: atof
functions.description: Converts a string into a floating-point number. Returns nil if the given string does not denote a number.

functions.name: atoi
functions.description: Converts a string into an integer. Returns nil if the given string does not denote an integer.

functions.name: atom
functions.description: Checks if an object is an atom.

functions.name: band
functions.description: Returns the integer result of the Boolean AND operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the & bitwise operator.

functions.name: bcdp
functions.description: Checks if an object is a binary primitive function.

functions.name: begin
functions.syntax: SKILL mode begin(  g_exp1  [ g_exp2 ...  g_expN ]  )  => g_result SKILL++ mode begin(  	def1  	[ def2 ...  		defN ]  )  => g_result
functions.description: In the SKILL mode, begin is a syntax form used to group a sequence of expressions. Evaluates expressions from left to right and returns the value of the last expression. Equivalent to progn. This expression type is used to sequence side effects such as input and output. Whereas, in the SKILL++ mode, begin is a syntax form used to group either a sequence of expressions or a sequence of definitions.

functions.name: bitfield
functions.description: Returns the value of a specified set of bits of a specified integer. Prefix form of the <:> operator.

functions.name: bitfield1
functions.description: Returns the value of a specified bit of a specified integer. Prefix form of the <> operator.

functions.name: blankstrp
functions.description: Checks if the given string is empty or has blank space characters only and returns true. If there are non-space characters blankstrp returns nil.

functions.name: bnand
functions.description: Returns the integer result of the Boolean NAND operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the ~& bitwise operator.

functions.name: bnor
functions.description: Returns the integer result of the Boolean NOR operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the ~| bitwise operator.

functions.name: bnot
functions.description: Returns the integer result of the Boolean NOT operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the ~ (one's complement) unary operator.

functions.name: booleanp
functions.description: Checks if an object is a boolean. Returns t if the object is t or nil. Returns nil otherwise.

functions.name: bor
functions.description: Returns the integer result of the Boolean OR operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the | bitwise operator.

functions.name: boundp
functions.description: Checks if the variable named by a symbol is bound, that is, has been assigned a value. The single argument form of boundp only works in SKILL mode.

functions.name: break
functions.description: Forces entry to the break handler if inserted directly into a SKILL function. The default break handler is the debugger.

functions.name: breakpt
functions.syntax: breakpt(  [ u_function  [ break_condition ] ]  ) where break_condition can be either (break_tag  g_condition  )  or  ( (break_tag  g_condition)...  ) => g_result
functions.description: Sets breakpoints on one or more functions or function objects.

functions.name: breakptMethod
functions.syntax: breakptMethod(  [ S_name ] [ l_specializer [ @before | @after | @around ] ] [ break_condition ]) where break_condition can be either (break_tag  g_condition  )  or  ( (break_tag  g_condition)...  ) => t / nil
functions.description: Sets breakpoint on the specified method's defmethod declaration.

functions.name: buildString
functions.description: Concatenates a list of strings with specified separation characters.

functions.name: bxnor
functions.description: Returns the integer result of the Boolean XNOR operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the ~^ bitwise operator.

functions.name: bxor
functions.description: Returns the integer result of the Boolean XOR operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the ^ bitwise operator.

functions.name: caar, caaar, caadr, cadr, caddr, cdar, cddr, ...
functions.syntax: ca|d[ a | d ][ a | d ][ a | d ] r(  l_list  )  => g_result
functions.description: Performs operations on a list using repeated applications of car and cdr. For example, caaar is equivalent to car( car( car( l_list))). The possible combinations are caaaar, caaadr, caadar, caaddr, caar, caddar, cadddr, cadr, cdaaar, cdaadr, cdaar, cdadar, cdaddr, cdadr, cdar, cddaar, cddadr, cddar, cdddar, cddddr, cdddr, cddr, caaar, caadr, cadar, caddr, cdadr, cadaar, cadadr, caddar, cadddr, cdaaar, cdaadr, cdadar, cdaddr, cddaar, cddadr, cdddar, and cddddr.

functions.name: callAs
functions.syntax: callAs(  us_class  s_genericFunction  g_arg1  [ g_arg2 ... ] )  => g_value
functions.description: Calls a method specialized for some super class of the class of a given object directly, bypassing the usual method inheritance and overriding of a generic function.

functions.name: callInitProc
functions.description: Calls all the initialization functions associated with a context.

functions.name: callNextMethod
functions.description: Calls the next applicable method for a generic function from within the current method. Returns the value returned by the method it calls.

functions.name: callUserAutoInitProc
functions.description: Calls the autoinit function for the given context name.

functions.name: car
functions.description: Returns the first element of a list. car is nondestructive, meaning that it returns the first element of a list but does not modify the list that was its argument.

functions.name: caseq
functions.syntax: caseq(  g_keyForm  l_clause1  [ l_clause2 ... ]  )  => g_result / nil
functions.description: Works like the case() function, but uses eq() to find a matching clause instead of the equal() function. The keys used with caseq() should therefore not be strings or lists. In case you want to use a string value or a list, SKILL recommends using the case() function. See eq for details on the difference between the eq() and equal() functions.

functions.name: catch
functions.description: Establishes a control transfer or a return point for the throw and err functions. The return point is identified with a s_tag. So, when a particular tag/exception is caught, catch evaluates g_form. If the forms execute normally (without error), the value of the last body form is returned from the catch. There can also be nested catch blocks and s_tag can be t (the value t  the catch function catch any condition thrown by throw).

functions.name: cdr
functions.description: Returns the tail of the list, that is, the list without its first element.

functions.name: cdsGetInstPath
functions.description: Returns the absolute path of the Cadence installation directory as a string. cdsGetInstPath is for the cds root hierarchy and is meant to be used by all Virtuoso and non-Virtuoso applications.

functions.name: cdsGetToolsPath
functions.description: Returns the absolute path of the Cadence installation tools directory as a string after resolving the tools directory appropriately. This function is provided for multiple platform support mainly to simplify access to a common Cadence installation hierarchy for all Unix platforms.

functions.name: cdsPlat
functions.description: Returns the platform for the Cadence software that is currently running. The possible values are: sun4v, sol86, hppa, ibmrs, wint, lnx86, or lni64.

functions.name: ceiling
functions.description: Returns the smallest integer not smaller than the given argument.

functions.name: changeClass
functions.description: Changes the class of the given instance (g_inst) to the specified class (g_className).

functions.name: changeWorkingDir
functions.description: Changes the working directory to the specified working directory.

functions.name: charToInt
functions.description: Returns the ASCII code of the first character of the given symbol. In SKILL, a single character symbol can be used as a character value.

functions.name: checkContextBit
functions.description: Checks and returns the context type of the specified context file.

functions.name: className
functions.description: Returns the class symbol denoting a class object.

functions.name: classOf
functions.description: Returns the class object of which the given object is an instance.

functions.name: classp
functions.description: Checks if the given object is an instance of the given class or is an instance of one of its subclasses.

functions.name: clear
functions.description: Clears all tracing and breakpoints.

functions.name: clearExitProcs
functions.description: Removes all registered exit procedures. When the optional argument g_tcovItem is set to t, it removes all exit procedures except those needed for the ilTCov reports.

functions.name: compareTime
functions.description: Compares two string arguments, representing a clock-calendar time.

functions.name: compress
functions.syntax: compress(  t_sourceFile  t_destFile  )  => t / error message
functions.description: Reduces the size of a SKILL file, which must be SKILL source code, and places the output into another file.

functions.name: concat
functions.description: Concatenates strings, symbols, or integers into a single symbol.

functions.name: cons
functions.description: Adds an element to the beginning of a list. Thus the car of l_result is g_element and the cdr of l_result is l_list. l_list can be nil, in which case a new list containing the single element is created.

functions.name: constar
functions.description: Adds elements to the beginning of a list.

functions.name: cont, continue
functions.description: Continues execution from a breakpoint. cont and continue are identical.

functions.name: copy
functions.description: Returns a copy of a list, that is, a list with all the top-level cells duplicated.

functions.name: copyDefstructDeep
functions.description: Performs a deep or recursive copy on defstructs with other defstructs as sub-elements, making copies of all the defstructs encountered.

functions.name: copy_<name>
functions.description: Creates and returns a copy of a structure. This function is created by the defstruct function where name is the name of the defstruct.

functions.name: count
functions.description: Counts the number of times a function has been called. This is an nlambda function. Returns the functions marked for counting.

functions.name: cputime
functions.description: Returns the total amount of CPU time (user and system) used in units of 60ths of a second.

functions.name: createDir
functions.description: Creates a directory.

functions.name: createDirHier
functions.description: Creates all directories specified in the given SKILL path that do not already exist

functions.name: csh
functions.description: Starts the UNIX C-shell as a process to execute a command string.

functions.name: debugQuit
functions.description: Exits one level of the SKILL debugger.

functions.name: debugStatus
functions.description: Prints the functions and variables being traced, functions that have breakpoints set, functions being counted, and the line breakpoints statistics.

functions.name: declare
functions.description: Creates an array with a specified number of elements. This is a syntax form. All elements of the array are initialized to unbound.

functions.name: declareLambda
functions.description: Tells the evaluator that certain (forward referenced) functions are of lambda type (as opposed to nlambda or macro).

functions.name: declareNLambda
functions.description: Tells the evaluator that certain (forward referenced) functions are of nlambda type (as opposed to lambdas or macros).

functions.name: declareSQNLambda
functions.description: Declares the given nlambda functions to be solely-quoting nlambdas.

functions.name: decode
functions.syntax: decode(  g_keyForm  l_clause1  [ l_clause2 ... ]  )  => g_result / nil
functions.description: Branches to one of the clauses depending on the value of the given expression. decode() evaluates g_keyForm and matches the resulting value sequentially against the clauses until it finds a match. Once a match is found it stops searching the clauses, evaluates the forms in the matching clause, and returns the resulting value.

functions.name: defCapDepends
functions.description: Specifies which contexts depend on which other contexts.

functions.name: defCapPrefixes
functions.description: Specifies which prefixes are acceptable for a context's global variables.

functions.name: defInitProc
functions.description: Registers a function that the system calls immediately after autoloading a context.

functions.name: defMathConstants
functions.description: Associates a set of predefined math constants as properties of the given symbol.

functions.name: defUserInitProc
functions.syntax: defUserInitProc(  t_contextName  u_func  [ autoInit ] ) => ( t_contextName s_procName )
functions.description: Registers a user-defined function that the system calls immediately after autoloading a context.

functions.name: defclass
functions.description: Creates a class object with class name and optional super class name (or names) and slot specifications. This is a macro form.

functions.name: defdynamic
functions.description: This syntax form sets the dynamic variable s_varName to g_value. In SKILL, this function works as a defvar. In Scheme, g_value is evaluated in the current lexical scope.

functions.name: defgeneric
functions.syntax: defgeneric(  s_functionName  ( s_arg1  [ s_arg2 ... ]  )  [ g_exp ... ]  )  => t
functions.description: Defines a generic function with an optional default method. This is a macro form. Be sure to leave a space after the function name.

functions.name: defglobalfun
functions.description: Defines a global function with the name and formal argument list you specify.

functions.name: define
functions.syntax: define(  s_var  g_expression  )  => s_var  define(  (  s_var  [ s_formalVar1 ... ]  )  g_body ...  )  => s_var
functions.description: (SKILL++ mode only) Is a syntax form used to provide a definition for a global or local variable. The define syntax form has two variations.

functions.name: define_syntax
functions.description: Creates a syntax rule using the syntax_rule expander form.

functions.name: defmacro
functions.description: Defines a macro which can take a list of formal arguments including @optional, @key, and @rest (instead of the more restrictive format as required by using mprocedure).

functions.name: defmethod
functions.syntax: defmethod(  s_name  (  ( s_arg1    s_class  )  s_arg2 ...  ) g_exp1 ... )  => t
functions.description: Defines a method for a given generic function. This is a macro form. Be sure to leave a space after s_name.

functions.name: defprop
functions.description: Adds properties to symbols but none of its arguments are evaluated. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: defsetf
functions.description: defsetf is a macro that allows you to specify an update function to use when setf() is called with a place using a given access function. It creates a macro with the prefix setf_ which is used by setf to update a value at the place given by s_accessFn().

functions.name: defstruct
functions.description: Creates a defstruct, a named structure that is a collection of one or more variables.

functions.name: defstructp
functions.description: Checks if an object is an instance of a particular defstruct.

functions.name: defun
functions.description: Defines a function with the name and formal argument list you specify. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: defvar
functions.description: Defines a variable and assign it a value.The variable defined follows the scoping rule.

functions.name: deleteDir
functions.description: Deletes the specified directory. The directory name can be specified with either an absolute or relative path; the SKILL path is used in the latter case. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

functions.name: deleteFile
functions.description: Deletes a file. The file name can be specified with either an absolute or relative path; the SKILL path is used in the latter case. If a symbolic link is passed in as the argument, it is the link itself, not the file or directory referenced by the link, that gets removed. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

functions.name: describe
functions.description: Prints information about the symbol s_symbol. If the symbol has a function definition, information on the argument list and other available details will be printed. If the symbol has a variable definition, information about its value and function will be printed. If the function is called without any arguments, the help message will be printed.

functions.name: destructuringBind
functions.description: Enables you to bind value to variables in a list. The list of values is obtained by evaluating the l_expression. The destructuringBind macro then evaluates the g_body form.

functions.name: difference
functions.description: Returns the result of subtracting one or more operands from the first operand. Prefix form of the - arithmetic operator.

functions.name: display
functions.description: Writes a representation of an object to the given port.

functions.name: do
functions.syntax: do(  (  (  s_var1  g_initExp1  [ g_stepExp1 ]  ) (  s_var2  g_initExp2  [ g_stepExp2 ]  ) ...  ) (  g_terminationExp  g_terminationExp1 ...  )             g_loopExp1              g_loopExp2 ...  ) => g_value
functions.description: Iteratively executes one or more expressions. Used in SKILL++ mode only.

functions.name: drain
functions.description: Writes out all characters that are in the output buffer of a port.

functions.name: dtpr
functions.description: Checks whether an object is a non-empty list.

functions.name: dump
functions.description: Prints the current value of all the local variables on the stack. SKILL++ variables are not displayed by this function. For SKILL++ use where to see the lexical bindings on the stack.

functions.name: dynamic
functions.description: This syntax form returns the value of the dynamic variable s_varName. If s_varName is not a dynamic variable, it returns an error.

functions.name: dynamicLet
functions.description: Evaluates the init forms (g_init1, g_init2, ...) in the current lexical environment, and then binds the variables (s_var1, s_var2, ...) in parallel. The variables are bound as SKILL dynamic variables for the duration of the body forms.

functions.name: ed
functions.description: Edits the named file.

functions.name: edi
functions.description: Edits the named file, then includes the file into SKILL.

functions.name: edit
functions.description: Edits a file, function, or variable. This function only works if you are in graphical mode. This is an nlambda function.

functions.name: edl
functions.description: Edits the named file, then loads the file into SKILL.

functions.name: encrypt
functions.description: Encrypts a SKILL file and places the output into another file.

functions.name: eq
functions.description: Checks addresses when testing for equality.

functions.name: equal
functions.description: Checks contents of strings and lists when testing for equality.

functions.name: eqv
functions.description: Tests for the equality between two strings or two numbers of the same type (for example, both numbers are integers). Except for numbers, eqv is like eq.

functions.name: err
functions.description: Causes an error.

functions.name: error
functions.description: Prints error messages and calls err.

functions.name: errset
functions.description: Encapsulates the execution of an expression in an environment safe from the error mechanism. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: errsetstring
functions.syntax: errsetstring(  t_string  [ g_errprint ]  [ s_langMode ]  )  => l_value / nil
functions.description: Reads and evaluates an expression stored in a string. Same as evalstring except that it calls errset to catch any errors that might occur during the parsing and evaluation.

functions.name: eval
functions.description: Evaluates an argument and returns its value. If an environment argument is given, g_expression is treated as SKILL++ code, and the expression is evaluated in the given (lexical) environment. Otherwise g_expression is treated as SKILL code.

functions.name: evalstring
functions.description: Reads and evaluates an expression stored in a string.

functions.name: evenp
functions.description: Checks if a number is an even integer.

functions.name: exists
functions.syntax: exists(  s_formalVar  l_valueList  g_predicateExpr  ) => g_result  exists(  s_key  o_table  g_predicateExpr  ) => t / nil
functions.description: Returns the first tail of l_valueList whose car satisfies a predicate expression. Also verifies whether an entry in an association table satisfies a predicate expression. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: existss
functions.syntax: existss(  s_formalVar  l_valueList  g_predicateExpr  ) => g_result  existss(  s_key  o_table  g_predicateExpr  ) => t / nil
functions.description: Returns the first tail of l_valueList whose car satisfies a predicate expression. Also verifies whether an entry in an association table satisfies a predicate expression. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable (s_formalVar) in a let block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart exists. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: exit
functions.description: Causes SKILL to exit with a given process status (defaults to 0), whether in interactive or batch mode.

functions.name: expandMacro
functions.description: Expands one level of macro call for a form.

functions.name: expandMacroDeep
functions.description: This function recursively expands all macros specified in g_form.

functions.name: expt
functions.description: Returns the result of raising a base number to a power. Prefix form of the ** exponentiation operator.

functions.name: fboundp
functions.description: Returns the function binding, if defined, for a specified function name.

functions.name: fdoc
functions.description: Returns the documentation string for the function bound to the symbol s_function. SKILL switch saveInlineDoc must be set to save and retrieve the doc string.

functions.name: fileLength
functions.description: Determines the number of bytes in a file.

functions.name: fileSeek
functions.syntax: fileSeek(  p_port  x_offset  x_whence  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Sets the position for the next operation to be performed on the file opened on a port. The position is specified in bytes.

functions.name: fileTell
functions.description: Returns the current offset in bytes for the file opened on a port.

functions.name: fileTimeModified
functions.description: Gets the time a given file was last modified.

functions.name: findClass
functions.description: Returns the class object associated with a symbol. The symbol is the symbolic name of the class object.

functions.name: findNamespace
functions.description: Returns the namespace object with the specified name.

functions.name: findSymbol
functions.description: Searches for a symbol that is specified as a string in the given namespace and returns its corresponding SKILL symbol.

functions.name: fix
functions.description: Returns the largest integer not larger than the given argument.

functions.name: fix2
functions.description: This function is a version of the fix function that works for rounding issue in floating-point calculations. The function returns the largest integer not larger than the given argument.

functions.name: fixp
functions.description: Checks whether the specified object is an integer, that is, a fixed number.

functions.name: flet
functions.description: Enables you to define local functions with LET semantics.

functions.name: float
functions.description: Converts a number into its equivalent floating-point number.

functions.name: floatp
functions.description: Checks whether the specified object is a floating-point number. Same as realp.

functions.name: floor
functions.description: Returns the largest integer not larger than the given argument.

functions.name: fndResetDb
functions.description: Resets a previously loaded Finder database.

functions.name: forall
functions.syntax: forall( s_formalVar l_valueList g_predicateExpr ) => t / nil forall( s_key o_table g_predicateExpr ) => t / nil
functions.description: Checks if g_predicateExpr evaluates to non-nil for every element in l_valueList. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: foralls
functions.syntax: foralls(  s_formalVar l_valueList g_predicateExpr ) => t / nil foralls( s_key o_table g_predicateExpr ) => t / nil
functions.description: Checks if g_predicateExpr evaluates to non-nil for every element in l_valueList. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable (s_formalVar) in a let block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart forall. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: foreachs
functions.syntax: foreachs(  s_formalVar  g_exprList  g_expr1  [ g_expr2 ... ]  ) => l_valueList / l_result  foreachs(  (  s_formalVar1...  s_formalVarN  )  g_exprList1...  g_exprListN  g_expr1  [ g_expr2 ... ]  ) => l_valueList / l_result  foreachs(  s_formalVar  g_exprTable  g_expr1  [ g_expr2 ... ]  ) => o_valueTable / l_result
functions.description: Evaluates one or more expressions for each element of a list of values. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable, s_formalVar,in a let block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart foreach. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: fors
functions.syntax: fors(  s_loopVar x_initialValue x_finalValue g_expr1 [ g_expr2 ... ] ) => t
functions.description: Evaluates the sequence g_expr1, g_expr2 ... for each loop variable value, beginning with x_initialValue and ending with x_finalValue. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable (s_loopVar) in a let() block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart for. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: fprintf
functions.description: Writes formatted output to a port.

functions.name: fscanf, scanf, sscanf
functions.syntax: fscanf(  p_inputPort  t_formatString  [ s_var1 ... ]  )  => x_items / nil  scanf(  t_formatString  [ s_var1 ... ]  )  => x_items / nil  sscanf(  t_sourceString  t_formatString  [ s_var1 ... ]  )  => x_items / nil
functions.description: The main difference between these functions is the source of input. fscanf reads input from a port according to format specifications and returns the number of items read in. scanf takes its input from piport implicitly. scanf only works in standalone SKILL when the piport is not the CIW. sscanf reads its input from a string instead of a port. Another difference is that whereas sscanf supports the width while reading floating-point numbers from the input string, fscanf and scanf do not.

functions.name: funcall
functions.description: Applies the given function to the given arguments.

functions.name: gc
functions.description: Forces a garbage collection. This function is also called by the system.

functions.name: gcsummary
functions.description: Prints a summary of memory allocation and garbage collection statistics in the current SKILL run.

functions.name: gensym
functions.description: Returns a new symbol based on the input argument.

functions.name: geqp
functions.description: This predicate function checks if the first argument is greater than or equal to the second argument. Prefix form of the >= operator.

functions.name: get
functions.description: Returns the value of a property in a property list (including disembodied property list), association table, structure, database object, and a standard object (instance of a user-defined subclass of standardObject). get has no infix operator syntax.

functions.name: getAllLoadedFiles
functions.description: Returns a list of all files loaded since debug mode was turned on.

functions.name: getApplicableMethods
functions.description: Returns a list of applicable methods (funObjects) for the specified generic function for a given set of arguments. The returned list contains methods in the calling order.

functions.name: getCallingFunction
functions.description: Returns the name of the calling function or procedure at the specified level in the call stack.

functions.name: getCompatContextVersion
functions.description: Returns the compatible context version (for IC 6.1.6/CAT 33.00, the compatible context version is 601).

functions.name: getCurSaveContextVersion
functions.description: Returns the current saveContext version (the version which the new context will have.) The possible return values are, 601 for compatible contexts and 602 for native contexts (for IC 6.1.6/CAT 33.00)

functions.name: getCurrentTime
functions.description: Returns a string representation of the current time.

functions.name: getDependents
functions.description: Returns a list of dependents registered for the given SKILL object, which could be a class or a generic function

functions.name: getDirFiles
functions.description: Returns a list of the names of all files and directories, including . and .., in a directory.

functions.name: getFnWriteProtect
functions.description: Checks if the given function is write-protected. The value is t if s_name is write-protected. Else, it is nil.

functions.name: getFunType
functions.description: Returns a symbol denoting the function type for a given function object. Possible function types include lambda, nlambda, macro, syntax, or primop.

functions.name: getFunctions
functions.description: Returns functions defined in a file loaded after debug mode is turned on.

functions.name: getGFbyClass
functions.description: Displays the list of all generic functions specializing on a given class.

functions.name: getGFproxy
functions.description: Returns a proxy instance from the specified generic function object

functions.name: getInstallPath
functions.description: Returns the absolute path of the Cadence DFII installation directory where the DFII products are installed on your system as a list of a single string.

functions.name: getLogin
functions.description: Returns the login name of the current user as a string.

functions.name: getMethodName
functions.description: Returns the method name for the given function object

functions.name: getMethodRole
functions.description: Returns the method role for the given function object. U_funObject should be a valid generic function object.

functions.name: getMethodSpec
functions.description: Returns the list of specializers for the given funobject.

functions.name: getMethodSpecializers
functions.description: Returns the specializers of all methods currently associated with the given generic function, in a list of class names. The first element in the list is t if there is a default method.

functions.name: getMuffleWarnings
functions.description: Returns a list of warnings that were called and suppressed by the preceding muffleWarnings command.

functions.name: getNativeContextVersion
functions.description: Returns the native context version (for IC 6.1.6/CAT 33.00, the native context version is 602).

functions.name: getOutstring
functions.description: Retrieves the content of the outstring port (while it is open).

functions.name: getPrompts
functions.description: Returns the current values of the first level and second level prompt text strings, respectively.

functions.name: getSG
functions.description: Evaluates and then retrieves the value of the specified attribute or property. It is a lambda implementation of getSGq().

functions.name: getShellEnvVar
functions.description: Returns the value of a UNIX environment variable, if it has been set. This function expands the environment variable name specified in the argument.

functions.name: getSkillPath
functions.description: Returns the current SKILL path. The SKILL path is used in resolving relative paths for some SKILL functions.

functions.name: getSkillVersion
functions.description: Returns the major version if the argument is left blank; otherwise, returns the current subversion (or tarkit version) of SKILL that is running in the build

functions.name: getSymbolNamespace
functions.description: Returns the namespace where the symbol is created.

functions.name: getTempDir
functions.description: Returns the system temp directory as a string.

functions.name: getVarWriteProtect
functions.description: (SKILL mode only) Checks if a variable is write-protected. Does not work in SKILL++ mode. In SKILL++ mode, use getFnWriteProtect instead.

functions.name: getVersion
functions.description: Returns the version number of the Cadence software you are currently using. If you specify the optional argument g_opt, as t (or a non-nil value), the subversion number of the Cadence software currently used is returned. By default, the full version number, including the hotfix version, of the Cadence software currently used is returned.

functions.name: getWarn
functions.description: Returns the buffered warning if it has not already been printed.

functions.name: getWorkingDir
functions.description: Returns the current working directory as a string.

functions.name: get_filename
functions.description: Returns the file name of a port.

functions.name: get_pname
functions.description: Returns the print name of a symbol as a string.

functions.name: get_string
functions.description: Converts the argument to a string if it is a symbol. Otherwise it returns the string itself.

functions.name: getc
functions.description: Reads and returns a single character from an input port. Unlike the C library, the getc and getchar SKILL functions are totally unrelated.

functions.name: getchar
functions.description: Returns an indexed character of a string or the print name if the string is a symbol. Unlike the C library, the getc and getchar SKILL functions are totally unrelated.

functions.name: getd
functions.description: Returns the function binding for a function name.

functions.name: getq
functions.syntax: getq(  sl_id  S_name  )  => g_result / nil  sl_id->S_name  => g_result / nil
functions.description: Returns the value of a property in a property list. Same as get except that the second argument is not evaluated. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: getqq
functions.syntax: getqq(  s_id  S_name  )  => g_result / nil  sl_id.S_name  => g_result / nil
functions.description: Returns the value of a property in a symbol's property list. Same as get except that neither argument is evaluated. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: globalProc
functions.description: Defines a global function using a formal argument list. The functions that you define using globalProc are defined within a lexical scope, but are globally accessible.

functions.name: go
functions.description: Transfers control to the statement following the label argument. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: greaterp
functions.description: This predicate function checks if the first argument is greater than the second argument. Prefix form of the > operator.

functions.name: help
functions.description: Retrieves and prints the cdsFinder documentation strings for the given function name (a symbol). If the given name is a string, it is interpreted as a regular expression, and the entire cdsFinder database is searched for functions whose name or documentation string contains or matches the given string. Help is an nlambda function.

functions.name: ilAddTopLevelErrorHandler
functions.description: Registers a new top-level error-handler. This error-handler is called after stacktrace, when an error occurs. If an error-handler already exists, the function displays a warning message.

functions.name: ilArgMatchesSpecializer
functions.syntax: ilArgMatchesSpecializer(  g_genericFunctionObj g_specObj g_argument ) => t / nil
functions.description: Determines whether a argument passed to the generic function at run time matches a particular specializer class, so that it then knows which method should be called.

functions.name: ilDebugCountLevels
functions.description: Returns the number of top-level debug and error frames present in the SKILL stack if SKILL is in breakpoint or error top level. Otherwise, the function returns 1.

functions.name: ilEquivalentSpecializers
functions.syntax: ilEquivalentSpecializers(  g_genericFunctionObj g_specObj1 g_specObj2 ) => t / nil
functions.description: Defines a method to check if two specializers are equal. This is required during method redefinition.

functions.name: ilGenerateSpecializer
functions.description: Returns a SKILL expression that makes an instance of the given specializer class and optionally set the slots. In the generated SKILL expression, l_argList can be used to initialize the slots.

functions.name: ilGetGFbyClass
functions.description: Returns a list of generic functions specializing on a given class.

functions.name: ilGetIdeSessionWindow
functions.description: Returns the SKILL IDE session window ID. If g_force is set to a value other than nil, the function creates an IDE window and displays it on the screen.

functions.name: ilGetTCovFiles
functions.description: Returns the list of files processed when you run an application in test coverage mode using the command line option -ilTCov <fileList>.

functions.name: ilMergeTCovData
functions.description: Merges tCov files from several directories and stores them in a single directory.

functions.name: ilRemoveMethod
functions.syntax: ilRemoveMethod(  s_genFunction  g_className  [ g_method ] )  => t / nil
functions.description: Removes a given method from a generic function.

functions.name: ilRemoveTopLevelErrorHandler
functions.description: Unregisters the top-level error handler previously registered by the ilAddTopLevelErrorHandler function.

functions.name: ilSlotBoundp
functions.description: Checks if a named slot is bound (has been assigned a value) to an instance.

functions.name: ilSpecMoreSpecificp
functions.syntax: ilSpecMoreSpecificp(  g_genericFunctionObj s_spec1 s_spec2 s_specArg ) => t / nil
functions.description: Checks if spec1 is more specific than spec2. You need to define all required ilSpecMoreSpecificp methods for all existing custom specializers (so that the system can find a method to compare any pair of custom specializers).

functions.name: ilToolBox
functions.description: Brings up the SKILL Development toolbox, which lets you debug SKILL programs using a form-based graphical user interface.

functions.name: ilgAddRecentFiles
functions.description: Adds the files listed in l_fileList to the SKILL IDE File menu.

functions.name: ilgAppendText
functions.description: Inserts text into the SKILL IDE editor window at the current cursor location.

functions.name: ilgCopy
functions.description: Copies the selected text into public text buffer. This function does not work on read-only files.

functions.name: ilgCut
functions.description: Cuts and pastes the selected text into public text buffer. This function does not work on read-only files.

functions.name: ilgFindIdent
functions.syntax: ilgFindIdent(  x_column  x_row  [ ?tab w_tab ] )  => l_coord / nil
functions.description: Returns the nearest identifiers from a given opening parenthesis location '(' in the SKILL IDE editor tab.

functions.name: ilgFindParenthesis
functions.syntax: ilgFindParenthesis(  x_column  x_row  [ ?level S_level ] [ ?direction S_direction ] [ ?tab w_tab ] )  => l_coord / nil
functions.description: Returns the closest parenthesis in a file currently open in the SKILL IDE editor.

functions.name: ilgFoldLine
functions.description: Folds a document block in SKILL IDE at (x_column x_row) where (x_column x_row) is the location of an opening parenthesis. If this function is called without arguments, the current cursor location is used for computing (x_column x_row).

functions.name: ilgGetCursorLocation
functions.description: Returns the location of the cursor in the SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgGetEditLock
functions.description: Returns the read-only property for a SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgGetHighlight
functions.description: Returns the list of highlight IDs for the text highlighted in the SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgGetSelectedLocation
functions.description: Returns the location coordinates of the current selection in the SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgGetText
functions.description: Returns the text between l_location_begin and l_location_end. If these locations are not provided, the entire text in the SKILL IDE editor window is returned.

functions.name: ilgInvokeIDE
functions.description: Displays the SKILL IDE main window.

functions.name: ilgLastDir
functions.description: Returns the directory path of the file currently open in SKILL IDE.

functions.name: ilgPaste
functions.description: Pastes the text from the clipboard/buffer to the cursor location in the SKILL IDE editor window. This function does not work on read-only files.

functions.name: ilgPositionInComment
functions.syntax: ilgPositionInComment(  x_column  x_row  [ ?tab w_tab ] )  => t / nil
functions.description: Checks if the specified coordinates (x_column x_row) fall within a comments block in the SKILL IDE document.

functions.name: ilgRegisterSelectionCB
functions.description: Registers a SKILL callback for SKILL IDE, which is called when some text is selected in the SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgResetErrorMarker
functions.description: Clears the error marker that was set by ilgSetErrorMarker() on line x_line in the SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgResetHighlight
functions.description: Resets a specified highlight in a SKILL IDE document between location l_location_begin and l_location_end.

functions.name: ilgResetWarningMarker
functions.description: Clears the warning marker that was set by ilgSetWarningMarker() on line x_line in the SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgRunSKILLIDE
functions.description: Launches SKILL IDE and opens the files listed in lt_fileList.

functions.name: ilgScrollToLocation
functions.description: Scrolls to the specified location in the specified SKILL IDE editor window or tab.

functions.name: ilgSearchText
functions.syntax: ilgSearchText(  t_text  [ ?loc l_location ] [ ?direction s_direction ] [ w_tab ] )  => l_location / nil
functions.description: Searches the specified text in a SKILL IDE document.

functions.name: ilgSelectText
functions.description: Selects the text between location l_location_begin and l_location_end in the SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgSetColor
functions.syntax: ilgSetColor(  t_text t_value [ x_alpha ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Sets a custom color for the given SKILL IDE GUI control.

functions.name: ilgSetCursorLocation
functions.description: Sets the cursor location in a SKILL IDE document.

functions.name: ilgSetEditLock
functions.description: Changes the read-only property for a SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgSetErrorMarker
functions.description: Sets the error marker with the pop-up description t_description on line x_line of the SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgSetHighlight
functions.syntax: ilgSetHighlight(  l_location_begin l_location_end t_color [ ?fullWidth g_fullWidth ] [ w_tab ] )  => l_highlightID / nil
functions.description: Highlights the area within l_location_begin and l_location_end in the color specified by t_color.

functions.name: ilgSetWarningMarker
functions.description: Sets the warning marker with pop-up description t_description on line x_line of the SKILL IDE editor window.

functions.name: ilgUnfoldLine
functions.description: This function unfolds a document block in SKILL IDE at position (x_column x_row), if it was folded. Here (x_column x_row) is the location of an opening parenthesis. If this function is called without arguments, the current cursor location is used for computing (x_column x_row).

functions.name: ilgUnregisterSelectionCB
functions.description: Unregisters a selection callback that was previously registered using ilgRegisterSelectionCB.

functions.name: importSkillVar
functions.description: (SKILL++ mode) Tells the compiler that the given variable names should be treated as SKILL global variables in SKILL++ code.

functions.name: importSymbol
functions.description: Imports symbols into the given namespace. By default, this function imports into the IL (or default) namespace.

functions.name: inNext
functions.description: Returns t if the function is called in the expression that is executed in the debugged code on the next() SKILL function.

functions.name: inScheme
functions.description: Evaluates a form as top-level SKILL++ code, disregarding the surrounding evaluation context.

functions.name: inSkill
functions.description: Evaluates a form as top-level SKILL code, disregarding the surrounding evaluation context.

functions.name: inStepOut
functions.description: Returns t if the function is called in the stepout() SKILL function.

functions.name: include
functions.description: Loads the file with name t_file in SKILL regardless of any errors in the file.

functions.name: index
functions.description: Returns a string consisting of the remainder of string1 beginning with the first occurrence of string2.

functions.name: info
functions.description: Prints the formatted output to poport according to the specification.

functions.name: initializeInstance
functions.syntax: initializeInstance(  g_instance  [ u_?initArg1    value1 ] [ u_?initArg2    value2 ]  ...  ) => t
functions.description: Initializes  the newly created instance of a class. The initializeInstance is a generic function which is called by the makeInstance function. Methods can be defined for a particular class to allow complex initialization to be performed on the object.

functions.name: inportp
functions.description: Checks if an object is an input port.

functions.name: installDebugger
functions.description: Installs the SKILL debugger as the error handler so that the debugger is entered automatically upon error.

functions.name: instring
functions.description: Opens a string for reading, just as infile would open a file.

functions.name: intToChar
functions.description: Returns the single-character symbol whose ASCII code is the given integer value.

functions.name: integerp
functions.description: Checks if an object is an integer. This function is the same as fixp.

functions.name: ipcActivateBatch
functions.description: Switches a child process to batch mode.

functions.name: ipcActivateMessages
functions.description: Switches a child process into interactive mode. In interactive mode, output from the child is written to a log file and is passed on to the parent process.

functions.name: ipcBatchProcess
functions.description: Invokes a process to execute batch commands. The child process in this case is a batch process that does not communicate with the parent process.

functions.name: ipcBeginProcess
functions.syntax: ipcBeginProcess(  t_command  [ t_hostName ]  [ tsu_dataHandler ]  [ tsu_errHandler ]  [ tsu_postFunc ]  [ t_logFile ]  )  => o_childId
functions.description: Invokes a process to execute a command or sequence of commands specified.

functions.name: ipcCloseProcess
functions.description: Closes the input channel of the child process.

functions.name: ipcContProcess
functions.description: Causes a suspended child process to resume executing. This is equivalent to sending a UNIX CONT signal.

functions.name: ipcGetExitStatus
functions.description: Returns the exit value of the child process.

functions.name: ipcGetPid
functions.description: Returns the runtime process identification number of the process executing this function.

functions.name: ipcGetPriority
functions.description: Gets the current default priority. If a child process handle is given, ipcGetPriority returns the priority under which the relevant child process was invoked.

functions.name: ipcIsActiveProcess
functions.description: Determines if a child process is active; that is, not stopped.

functions.name: ipcIsAliveProcess
functions.description: Checks if a child process is still alive.

functions.name: ipcKillAllProcesses
functions.description: Kills every process initiated by the parent through one of the ipcBeginProcess class of functions.

functions.name: ipcKillProcess
functions.description: Kills the process identified by o_childId. This call results in a UNIX SIGKILL signal being sent to the child process.

functions.name: ipcReadProcess
functions.description: Reads data from the child process stdout channel, allowing the developer to specify a time, in seconds, beyond which the read operation must not block. It only reads 4096 bytes for each call.

functions.name: ipcSetPriority
functions.description: Sets the priority value for child processes. All processes spawned after this call run at the priority offset to x_priorityChange.

functions.name: ipcSignalProcess
functions.description: Sends the specified POSIX signal to the specified UNIX/Linux child process.

functions.name: ipcSkillProcess
functions.syntax: ipcSkillProcess(  t_command  [ t_hostName ]  [ tsu_dataHandler ]  [ tsu_errHandler ]  [ tsu_postFunc ]  [ t_logFile ]  [ x_cmdDesc ]  [ x_resDesc ]  ) => o_childId
functions.description: Invokes an operating system process capable of executing SKILL functions in the parent process and opens two additional channels to the child process that let the child send and receive the results of SKILL commands.

functions.name: ipcSleep
functions.description: Causes the parent process to be delayed for the given number of seconds.

functions.name: ipcSleepMilli
functions.description: Causes the parent process to be delayed for the given number of milliseconds. Use the otherwise identical ipcSleep function to specify the delay in seconds.

functions.name: ipcSoftInterrupt
functions.description: Equivalent to executing the UNIX kill -2 command. If the child process is active, it is sent a soft interrupt. The child is responsible for catching the signal.

functions.name: ipcStopProcess
functions.description: Causes the child process to suspend its execution. This is equivalent to sending a STOP signal through the UNIX kill command.

functions.name: ipcWait
functions.description: Causes the parent process to suspend until the child terminates.

functions.name: ipcWaitForProcess
functions.description: Causes the parent process to suspend until the child process is alive and ready for communication.

functions.name: ipcWriteProcess
functions.description: Writes data to the stdin port of the child process.

functions.name: isCallable
functions.description: Checks if a function is defined or is autoloadable from a context.

functions.name: isClass
functions.description: Checks if the given object is a class object.

functions.name: isContextLoaded
functions.description: Returns t if a context file with the given base name has been loaded into the current session.

functions.name: isDir
functions.description: Checks if a path exists and if it is a directory name.

functions.name: isExecutable
functions.description: Checks if you have permission to execute a file or search a directory.

functions.name: isFile
functions.description: Checks if a file exists and that it is not a directory.

functions.name: isFileEncrypted
functions.description: Checks if a file exists and is encrypted.

functions.name: isFileName
functions.description: Checks if a file or directory exists.

functions.name: isGeneric
functions.description: Checks if the specified symbol (function name) or funobj (function object) represents a generic SKILL++ function.

functions.name: isInfinity
functions.description: Checks whether the given flownum argument represents infinity (positive or negative).

functions.name: isLargeFile
functions.description: Checks if a file is a large file (with size greater than 2GB).

functions.name: isLink
functions.description: Checks if a path exists and if it is a symbolic link.

functions.name: isMacro
functions.description: Checks if the given symbol denotes a macro.

functions.name: isNaN
functions.description: Checks whether the given flownum argument represents NaN (not-a-number). Else, it returns nil.

functions.name: isPortAtEOF
functions.description: Takes an input port and returns t if end-of-file (EOF) has previously been detected while reading the input port; it returns nil otherwise.

functions.name: isReadable
functions.description: Checks if you have permission to read a file or list a directory. Uses the current SKILL path for relative paths. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

functions.name: isVarImported
functions.description: Checks if the specified variable was imported into SKILL++ or not.

functions.name: isWritable
functions.description: Checks if you have permission to write to a file or update a directory. Uses the current SKILL path for relative paths. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

functions.name: labels
functions.description: Enables you to define local functions with LET semantics.

functions.name: lambda
functions.description: Defines a function without a name. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: last
functions.description: Returns the last list cell in a list.

functions.name: lconc
functions.description: Uses a tconc structure to efficiently splice a list to the end of another list.

functions.name: leftshift
functions.description: Returns the integer result of shifting a value a specified number of bits to the left. Prefix form of the << arithmetic operator. leftshift is logical (that is, vacated bits are 0-filled).

functions.name: length
functions.description: Determines the length of a list, array, association table, or string.

functions.name: leqp
functions.description: This predicate function checks if the first argument is less than or equal to the second argument. Prefix form of the <= operator.

functions.name: lessp
functions.description: This predicate function checks if the first argument is less than the second argument. Prefix form of the < operator.

functions.name: let
functions.syntax: SKILL mode let(  l_bindings  g_expr1 ...  )  => g_result  SKILL++ mode let(  [ s_var ] 	( 		( s_var1 s_initExp1 ) 		( s_var2 s_initExp2 ) 	... 	) body ) => g_result
functions.description: In the SKILL mode, this function provides a faster alternative to prog for binding local variables only. This is a syntax form. In the SKILL++ mode, this function declares a lexical scope. This includes a collection of local variables, as well as body expressions to be evaluated. This becomes a named let if the optional s_var is given.

functions.name: letrec
functions.syntax: letrec( 	( 		( s_var1 s_initExp1 ) 		( s_var2 s_initExp2 ) 	...  	) body )  => g_result
functions.description: (SKILL++ mode) A letrec expression can be used in SKILL++ mode only. All the bindings are in effect while their initial values are being computed, thus allowing mutually recursive definitions. Use letrec to declare recursive local functions.

functions.name: letseq
functions.syntax: letseq( 	( 		( s_var1 initExp1 ) 		( s_var2 initExp2 )  		... 	) body ) => g_result
functions.description: A letseq expression can be used in both SKILL and SKILL++ modes. The bindings and evaluations are performed sequentially.

functions.name: lindex
functions.syntax: lindex(  l_list  g_element  [ ?all g_all ] )  => x_result / l_result / nil
functions.description: Returns the index number of the given element in l_list.

functions.name: lineread
functions.description: Parses the next line in the input port into a list that you can further manipulate. It is used by the interpreter's top level to read in all input and understands SKILL and SKILL++ syntax.

functions.name: linereadstring
functions.description: Executes lineread on a string and returns the first form read in. Anything after the first form is ignored.

functions.name: list
functions.description: Creates a list with the given elements.

functions.name: listAlias
functions.description: Prints a (property) list of all current aliases and associated function symbols, or the function symbol for which the given alias is defined.

functions.name: listFunctions
functions.description: Returns all public function names that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression. If the second (optional) argument is specified as t (or a non-nil value), listFunctions looks at the SKILL virtual machine, rather than the cdsFinder database, and returns all isCallable Cadence public functions and user-defined SKILL functions that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression.

functions.name: listToVector
functions.description: Returns a vector (array) filled with the elements from the given list. A vector is represented by an array.

functions.name: listVariables
functions.description: Returns all variable names that match the given substring or regular expression as part or all of their print name.

functions.name: listp
functions.description: Checks whether the specified object is a list.

functions.name: loadContext
functions.syntax: loadContext(  t_contextFileName  [ g_ignore64bitSubpath ] )  => t / nil / error
functions.description: Loads a context file into the current session.

functions.name: loadPort
functions.syntax: loadPort(  p_port  [?langMode g_langMode] [?password g_password] [?ignoreErrors g_ignoreErrors]) )  => t
functions.description: Loads a SKILL file from p_port.

functions.name: loadTopContextForms
functions.syntax: loadTopContextForms(  t_FileName  [ ?debugMode g_debugMode ]  [ ?writeProtect g_writeProtect ]  [ ?writeProtectAll g_writeProtectAll ]  [ ?lazyComp g_lazyComp ]  [ ?printinfix g_printinfix ]  [ ?integermode g_integermode ]  [ ?mergemode g_mergemode ]  [ ?readProtect g_readProtect ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Loads top-level SKILL or Scheme forms from a file. If the setContext mode is set, these forms are saved in a context. After the context is loaded, these forms are evaluated at the top-level, as if these were loaded from an .il or .ils file.

functions.name: loadi
functions.description: Identical to load, except that loadi ignores errors encountered during the load, prints an error message, and then continues loading.

functions.name: loadstring
functions.description: Opens a string for reading, then parses and executes expressions stored in the string, just as load does in loading a file.

functions.name: lowerCase
functions.description: Returns a string that is a copy of the given argument with uppercase alphabetic characters replaced by their lowercase equivalents.

functions.name: lsprintf
functions.description: Returns a string according to the provided format. lsprintf is a lambda version of the sprintf function that can be used as an argument with apply or funcall.

functions.name: makeInstance
functions.syntax: makeInstance(  us_class  [ u_?initArg1    value1 ] [ u_?initArg2    value2 ] ...  ) => g_instance
functions.description: Creates an instance of a class, which can be given as a symbol or a class object.

functions.name: makeNamespace
functions.description: Creates a SKILL namespace with the given t_name. A namespace or its parts can be saved in a context and loaded with the context.

functions.name: makeSymbol
functions.description: Creates a symbol corresponding to the specified symbol or character string. You can optionally specify the namespace name (t_namespace) in which you want to create the symbol.

functions.name: makeTable
functions.description: Creates an empty association table.

functions.name: makeTempFileName
functions.description: Appends a string suffix to the last component of a path template so that the resulting composite string does not duplicate any existing file name.

functions.name: makeVector
functions.description: Creates an array (vector) with the specified number of elements, and optionally initializes each entry.

functions.name: make_<name>
functions.description: Creates an instance of a defstruct specified by name.

functions.name: map
functions.description: Applies the given function to successive sublists of the argument lists and returns the first argument list. All of the lists should have the same length. This function is not the same as the standard Scheme map function. To get the behavior of the standard Scheme map function, use mapcar instead. This function is usually used for its side effects, not its return value (see mapc).

functions.name: mapc
functions.description: Applies a function to successive elements of the argument lists and returns the first argument list. All of the lists should have the same length. mapc returns l_arg1.

functions.name: mapcan
functions.description: Applies a function to successive elements of the argument lists and returns the result of appending these intermediate results. All of the lists should have the same length.

functions.name: mapcar
functions.description: Applies a function to successive elements of the argument lists and returns the list of the corresponding results.

functions.name: mapcon
functions.description: Applies the function u_func to successive sublists of the lists and returns a concatenated list.

functions.name: mapinto
functions.description: Applies g_function to the elements of l_sequences and destructively modifies the l_resultSequence. The first argument is a sequence that receives the results of the mapping. If l_resultSequence and the other argument sequences are not all of the same length, the mapping stops when the shortest of l_resultSequence or l_sequences is exhausted.

functions.name: maplist
functions.description: Applies a function to successive sublists of the argument lists and returns a list of the corresponding results. All of the lists should have the same length.

functions.name: measureTime
functions.description: Measures the time needed to evaluate an expression and returns a list with performance data (n_utime, n_stime, n_clockTime, and x_pageFaults) for the executed expressions. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: member, memq, memv
functions.syntax: member(  g_obj  g_arg  )  => l_sublist / t / nil
functions.description: Returns the largest sublist of l_list whose first element is g_obj or checks whether the key g_obj exists in the association table. For comparison, member uses the equal function, memq uses the eq function, and memv uses eqv.

functions.name: memoryAllocated
functions.description: Returns the amount of memory allocated by a process. The returned value is an approximation in megabytes and might not include the memory that has been allocated, but the amount that is unused.

functions.name: minus
functions.description: Returns the negative of a number. Prefix form of the - unary operator.

functions.name: minusp
functions.description: Checks if a value is a negative number. Same as negativep.

functions.name: modf
functions.description: Returns the floating-point remainder of the division of f_flonum1 by f_flonum2.

functions.name: modulo
functions.description: Returns the remainder of dividing two integers. The remainder always has the sign of the divisor.

functions.name: mprocedure
functions.description: Defines a macro with the given name that takes a single formal argument. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: muffleWarnings
functions.description: Returns the result of the last expression evaluated. If the last expression evaluated calls the warn function (either SKILL warn() or C-level ilWarn*), the related message is not printed out.

functions.name: nconc
functions.description: Equivalent to a destructive append where the first argument is modified.

functions.name: ncons
functions.description: Builds a list containing an element. This function is equivalent to cons( g_element nil ).

functions.name: nearlyEqual
functions.syntax: nearlyEqual(  n_val1 n_val2  [ f_relTolerance [f_absTolerance] ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Checks whether one value (n_val1) is approximately equal to another value (n_val2).

functions.name: needNCells
functions.description: Ensures that there is enough memory available for the specified number of SKILL objects (cells).

functions.name: negativep
functions.description: Checks whether the specified value is a negative number. Same as minusp.

functions.name: neq
functions.description: Checks if two arguments are not identical using the eq function and returns t if they are not. That is, g_arg1 and g_arg2 are tested to see if they are at the same address in memory.

functions.name: nequal
functions.description: Checks if two arguments are not logically equivalent using the equal function and returns t if they are not.

functions.name: next
functions.description: Allows execution to proceed until the next expression. This function only works if executed from within a break handler and if the code you want to step through was loaded under debugMode. See installDebugger.

functions.name: nextMethodp
functions.description: Checks if there is a next applicable method for the current method's generic function. The current method is the method that is calling nextMethodp.

functions.name: nindex
functions.description: Finds the symbol or string, S_string2, in t_string1 and returns the character index, starting from one, of the first point at which the S_string2 matches part of t_string1.

functions.name: nlambda
functions.description: (SKILL mode only) Allows nlambda functions to be defined without having names. In all other respects, nlambda is identical to nprocedure. This is a syntax form that is not supported in SKILL++ mode.

functions.name: not
functions.description: Same as the ! operator. Returns t if the object is nil, and returns nil otherwise.

functions.name: nprocedure
functions.description: (SKILL mode only) Defines an nlambda function with a function name and a single formal argument. This is a syntax form that is not supported in SKILL++ mode.

functions.name: nth
functions.description: Returns an index-selected element of a list, assuming a zero-based index.

functions.name: nthcdr
functions.description: Applies cdr to a list a given number of times.

functions.name: nthelem
functions.description: Returns the indexed element of the list, assuming a one-based index.

functions.name: null
functions.description: Checks if an object is equal to nil.

functions.name: numOpenFiles
functions.description: Returns the number of files now open and the maximum number of files that a process can open. The numbers are returned as a two-element list.

functions.name: numberp
functions.description: Checks if a data object is a number, that is, either an integer or floating-point number.

functions.name: oddp
functions.description: Checks whether an object is an odd integer. oddp is a predicate function.

functions.name: onep
functions.description: Checks whether the given object is equal to one. onep is a predicate function.

functions.name: openportp
functions.description: Checks if the given argument is a port object and it is open (for input or output), nil otherwise.

functions.name: or
functions.syntax: or(  g_arg1  g_arg2  [ g_arg3... ]  )  => nil / g_val
functions.description: Evaluates from left to right its arguments to see if the result is non-nil. As soon as an argument evaluates to non-nil, or returns that value without evaluating the rest of the arguments. If all arguments except the last evaluate to nil, or returns the value of the last argument as the result of the function call. Prefix form of the || binary operator.

functions.name: otherp
functions.description: Checks if an object is a user type object, such as an association table or a window.

functions.name: outportp
functions.description: Checks if an object is an output port.

functions.name: outstring
functions.description: Takes no arguments and returns an opened output port for strings (or an outport). After a port is opened, it can be used with functions, such as fprintf, println, and close that write to an output port. You need to use the getOutstring function to retrieve the content of output port (while it is open).

functions.name: outstringp
functions.description: Checks whether the specified value is an outstring port.

functions.name: pairp
functions.description: Checks if an object is a cons object, that is, a non-empty list. This function is equivalent to dtpr.

functions.name: parseString
functions.description: Breaks a string into a list of substrings with break characters.

functions.name: pcreCompile
functions.description: Compiles a regular expression string pattern (t_pattern) into an internal representation that you can use in a pcreExecute function call. The compilation method is PCRE/Perl-compatible. You can use a second (optional) argument to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compilation. You can set and unset the PCRE_CASELESS, PCRE_MULTILINE, PCRE_DOTALL, and PCRE_EXTENDED independent option bits from within the pattern. The content of the options argument specifies the initial setting at the start of compilation. You can set the PCRE_ANCHORED option at matching time and at compile time.

functions.name: pcreExecute
functions.syntax: pcreExecute(  o_comPatObj  S_subject  [ x_options ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Matches the subject string or symbol (S_subject) against a previously compiled pattern set up by the last pcreCompile call (o_comPatObj). The matching algorithm is PCRE/Perl-compatible. You can use a third (optional) argument to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern matching. You can use this function in conjunction with pcreCompile to match several subject strings or symbols against a single pattern.

functions.name: pcreGenCompileOptBits
functions.syntax: pcreGenCompileOptBits(  [ ?caseLess  g_setCaseLessp ] [ ?multiLine g_setMultiLinep ] [ ?dotAll    g_setDotAllp ] [ ?extended  g_setExtendedp ] [ ?anchored  g_setAnchoredp ] [ ?dollar_endonly g_setDollarEndonlyp ] [ ?ungreedy  g_setUngreedyp ] [ ?no_auto_capture g_setNoAutoCapturep ] [ ?firstline g_setFirstlinep ] )  => x_resultOptBits
functions.description: Generates bitwise inclusive OR-bor()-of zero or more independent option bits that affect compilation so that you can specify them symbolically in the pcreCompile function. If you call pcreGenCompileOptBits with no arguments, the function returns a zero (options have their default settings).

functions.name: pcreGenExecOptBits
functions.syntax: pcreGenExecOptBits(  [ ?anchored g_setAnchoredp ] [ ?notbol   g_setNotbolp ] [ ?noteol   g_setNoteolp ] [ ?notempty g_setNotemptyp ] [ ?partial  g_setPartialp ] ) => x_resultOptBits
functions.description: Generates bitwise inclusive OR-bor()-of zero or more independent option bits that affect pattern matching so that you can specify them symbolically in the pcreExecute function. If you call pcreGenExecOptBits with no arguments, the function returns a zero (options have their default settings).

functions.name: pcreGetRecursionLimit
functions.description: Returns the PCRE maximum recursion depth (stack depth) that is set by the pcreSetRecursionLimit() function. The default value is 10000000.

functions.name: pcreListCompileOptBits
functions.description: Displays information about the options used with pcreGenCompileOptBits. See the description of pcreGenCompileOptBits for more information.

functions.name: pcreListExecOptBits
functions.description: Displays information about the options used with pcreGenExecOptBits.

functions.name: pcreMatchAssocList
functions.syntax: pcreMatchAssocList(  g_pattern  l_subjects  [ x_compOptBits ]  [ x_execOptBits ] )  => l_results / nil / error message(s)
functions.description: Matches the keys of an association list of subjects (strings or symbols) against a regular expression pattern (g_pattern) and returns an association list of those elements that match. The keys are the first elements of each key/value pair in the association list. You can use optional arguments to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compiling and matching. The compiling and matching algorithms are PCRE/Perl-compatible.

functions.name: pcreMatchList
functions.syntax: pcreMatchList(  g_pattern  l_subjects  [ x_compOptBits ]  [ x_execOptBits ] )  => l_results / nil / error message(s)
functions.description: Matches a list of subjects (strings or symbols) against a regular expression pattern (g_pattern) and returns a list of those elements that match. You can use optional arguments to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compiling and matching. The compiling and matching algorithms are PCRE/Perl-compatible.

functions.name: pcreMatchp
functions.syntax: pcreMatchp(  g_pattern  S_subject  [ x_compOptBits ]  [ x_execOptBits ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Checks to see whether the subject string or symbol (S_subject) matches the specified regular expression pattern (g_pattern). You can use optional arguments to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compiling and matching. The compiling and matching algorithms are PCRE/Perl-compatible. For greater efficiency when matching a number of subjects against a single pattern, you should use pcreCompile and pcreExecute.

functions.name: pcreObjectp
functions.description: Checks to see whether the given argument is a pcreObject or not.

functions.name: pcrePrintLastMatchErr
functions.description: Prints the error message associated with the last failed matching operation (that is, when pcreExecute returns nil).

functions.name: pcreReplace
functions.syntax: pcreReplace(  o_comPatObj  t_source  t_replacement  x_index  [ x_options ] )  => t_result / t_source
functions.description: Replaces one or all occurrences of a previously-compiled regular expression in the given source string with the specified replacement string. The integer index indicates which of the matching substrings to replace. If the index is less than or equal to zero, the function applies the replacement string to all matching substrings. You can use an optional argument to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern matching. The matching algorithm is PCRE/Perl-compatible.

functions.name: pcreSetRecursionLimit
functions.description: Sets the maximum recursion depth for SKILL/PCRE match algorithms. The maximum recursion depth needs to be set for systems that have a low stack depth, in order to prevent crashes while using SKILL PCRE functions.

functions.name: pcreSubpatCount
functions.description: Counts the subpatterns in a PCRE pattern.

functions.name: pcreSubstitute
functions.description: If o_pcreObject is not provided, pcreSubstitute copies the input string and substitutes all pattern tags in it using the corresponding matched strings from the last pcreExecute/pcreMatch* operation.

functions.name: phoIPCGetMessageProcessor
functions.description: Returns the name of the message processor associated with the specified tool.

functions.name: phoIPCGetServerCheck
functions.description: Returns the name of the registered function that can be called to check if the server associated with the specified tool is operating correctly.

functions.name: phoIPCProcessMarkers
functions.syntax: phoIPCProcessMarkers( d_cellviewID l_markerList s_displayToolName ) => t / nil
functions.description: Specifies the default marker processor for the specified tool and generates markers in the Annotation Browser assistant, categorizing the markers based on the specified markerList.

functions.name: phoIPCProcessPorts
functions.syntax: phoIPCProcessPorts( d_cellviewID l_opticalPortList [ l_portMap ] [ l_lppMap ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Creates optical ports in the specified cellview using the specfied portList. This is the default optical port processor.

functions.name: phoIPCProcessServerMessage
functions.syntax: phoIPCProcessServerMessage( d_cellviewID t_waveguideLayer t_serverMessage [ g_dropPorts ] [ l_portMap ] [ l_lppMap ] )
functions.description: Issues messages from the IPC processor, which can further be used in Pcells to create geometries.

functions.name: phoIPCProcessShapes
functions.syntax: phoIPCProcessShapes( d_cellviewID l_shapeList l_portMap [ l_lppMap ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Uses shapeList to create shapes and electrical pins in the specified cellview. This is the default shape processor.

functions.name: phoIPCRegisterMessageProcessor
functions.description: Registers the message processor corresponding to the specified tool. In addition, the function ensures that the message processor function is defined and has the correct number of arguments.

functions.name: phoIPCRegisterServerCheck
