You can align objects that are at different levels of hierarchy as long as both objects are in the same top-level layout cellview. You can specify positive or negative separation between alignment points in the direction of both the X and Y axes, either as absolute distances or with Cadence SKILL language expressions. The system applies the offset from the reference point or reference object to the object to be aligned.

functions.name: rodAssignHandleToParameter
functions.syntax: rodAssignHandleToParameter(		 [ ?parameter S_parameter ] [ ?rodObj R_rodObj ] [ ?handleName Sl_handleName ] [ ?displayName S_displayName ] [ ?displayExpression S_displayExpression ] [ ?stretchDir S_stretchDir ] [ ?stretchType S_stretchType ] [ ?moveOrigin g_moveOrigin ] [ ?updateIncrement f_updateIncrement ] [ ?userData g_userData ] [ ?userFunction Sl_userFunction ] [ ?stretchKey S_stretchKey ] [ ?shape S_shape ] );end rodAssignHandleToParameter => t / nil
functions.description: Assigns one or more user- or system-defined point handles on a ROD object within a SKILL-based parameterized cell (Pcell) to a single Pcell parameter, so you can change the value of the parameter by graphically stretching the handle(s). Stretching a handle has the same effect as changing the value of the associated parameter for the Pcell instance using the Edit Properties form. You cannot stretch handles on the Pcell master. All rodAssignHandleToParameter statements must occur within the body-of-code section of a SKILL-based Pcell.

functions.name: rodCheck
functions.syntax: rodCheck(		 d_cvID  [ g_createMarkers ] ); end rodCheck => Rl_rodObj
functions.description: Searches the specified cellview for multipart paths (MPPs) for which the geometry does not match the definition information, and returns a list of the ROD object IDs. The MPPs found by this function include those that have lost their subshape definition information. By default, this function places warning markers over the potentially affected MPPs. (If you do not want to see warning markers, set the g_createMarkers argument to nil.) Although subparts with missing definition information are still visible graphically, their definitions have been deleted from the database. Editing an affected MPP causes an immediate loss of the subpart graphics.

functions.name: rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView
functions.syntax: rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView(		 t_libName  t_cellName  t_viewName  g_fix  g_createMarkers ); end rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView => l_defectiveMPPIds / nil
functions.description: Finds and opens the design specified by t_libName, t_cellName, and t_viewName, and checks if any MPP in the design contains defective internal data. If MPPs containing defective internal data are found, rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView fixes them and creates markers on them depending on the values of g_fix and g_createMarkers arguments.

functions.name: rodCheckMPPs
functions.syntax: rodCheckMPPs(		 d_cellViewId  R_rodObj | list(R_rodObj ...)  g_fix  g_createMarkers );end rodCheckMPPs => l_defectiveMPPIds / nil
functions.description: Checks if the given list of multipart paths (MPPs) contains corrupt internal data. If MPPs containing defective internal data are found, rodCheckMPPs fixes or creates markers to highlight them, or does both.

functions.name: rodCoordBisect
functions.description: Divides the input value by two (bisect). You can optionally set the argument that rounds off the calculated value, truncates it, or converts it based on the defined maximum ceiling.

functions.name: rodCoordCreate
functions.syntax: rodCoordCreate( g_inputValue [ S_unitType [ S_snapType ] ] [ x_resolution ] );end rodCoordCreate => o_rodCoordObj
functions.description: Creates a rodCoord object from the given value, that is, g_inputValue.

functions.name: rodCoordDefineGrid
functions.description: Defines the grid and the arithmetic resolution factor values, which are used by the rodCoord* API.

functions.name: rodCoordFix
functions.description: Fixes the rodCoord object and returns a new rodCoord object using the fix() SKILL function.

functions.name: rodCoordGetGrid
functions.description: Returns the grid value (defined by rodCoordDefineGrid) as a rodCoord object.

functions.name: rodCoordIsOnGrid
functions.syntax: rodCoordIsOnGrid( o_rodCoord [ n_gridValue ] );end rodCoordIsOnGrid => t / nil
functions.description: Checks if the data in the given rodCoord object is on the grid or not.

functions.name: rodCoordParseString
functions.description: Creates a rodCoord object out of t_rodString generated by the rodCoordToString function.

functions.name: rodCoordPartition
functions.description: Performs a division on the given arguments - dividend and divisor.

functions.name: rodCoordSnap
functions.syntax: rodCoordSnap( o_rodCoord [[ S_snapType ]  [ n_gridValue ]] );end rodCoordSnap => o_rodCoord
functions.description: Snaps a rodCoord object so that its value is on the grid.

functions.name: rodCoordToFloat
functions.description: Returns the rodCoord data in user unit as floating point number.

functions.name: rodCoordToInt
functions.description: Returns the rodCoord data in user unit as a fixed number.

functions.name: rodCoordToString
functions.description: Returns a string containing the rodCoord data in user unit as floating number.

functions.name: rodCreateHandle
functions.syntax: rodCreateHandle(	 [ ?name S_name ] [ ?type S_type ] [ ?value g_value ] [ ?rodObj R_rodObj ] );end rodCreateHandle => t / nil
functions.description: Creates a user-defined handle for any ROD object (named shape, instance, or cellview); the object must be at level zero in the hierarchy. For example, you can create a handle for polyRect or for instance I1, but not for I1/polyRect.

functions.name: rodCreatePath
functions.syntax: rodCreatePath(	 [ ?name S_name] [ ?layer txl_layer ] [ ?width n_width ] [ ?pts l_pts ] [ ?justification S_justification ] [ ?offset n_offset ] [ ?endType S_endType ] [ ?beginExt n_beginExt ] [ ?endExt n_endExt ] [ ?choppable g_choppable ] [ ?cvId d_cvId ] [ ?fromObj Rl_fromObj ] [ ?size txf_size ] [ ?startHandle l_startHandle ] [ ?endHandle l_endHandle ] [ ?prop l_prop ] 	 [rodConnectivityArgs...  ] 	;start ROD Connectivity Arguments (rodConnectivityArgs) 	[ ?netName S_netName ] 	[ ?termName S_termName ] 	[ ?termIOType S_termIOType ] 	[ ?pin g_pin ] 	[ ?pinAccessDir tl_pinAccessDir ] 	[ ?pinLabel g_pinLabel ] 	[ ?pinLabelHeight n_pinLabelHeight ] 	[ ?pinLabelLayer txl_pinLabelLayer ] 	[ ?pinLabelFont S_pinLabelFont ] 	[ ?pinLabelDrafting g_pinLabelDrafting ] 	[ ?pinLabelOrient S_pinLabelOrient ] 	[ ?pinLabelOffsetPoint l_pinLabelOffsetPoint ] 	[ ?pinLabelJust S_pinLabelJust ] 	[ ?pinLabelRefHandle S_pinLabelRefHandle ] 	;end ROD Connectivity Arguments  [ ?offsetSubPath            l_offsetSubpathArgs... ] ;start Offset Subpath Arguments (l_offsetSubpathArgs) list( 	list( 		[ ?layer txl_layer ] 		[ ?width n_width ] 		[ ?choppable g_choppable ] 		[ ?sep n_sep ] 		[ ?justification S_justification ] 		[ ?beginOffset n_beginOffset ] 		[ ?endOffset n_endOffset ] 		[ ?prop l_prop ] 		;repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here 	);end first offset subpath list 		... 	);end offset subpath lists ;end Offset Subpath Arguments  [ ?encSubPath        l_encSubpathArgs...  ] ;start Enclosure Subpath Arguments (l_encSubpathArgs) list( 	list( 		[ ?layer txl_layer ] 		[ ?enclosure n_enclosure ] 		[ ?choppable g_choppable ]	 		[ ?beginOffset n_beginOffset ] 		[ ?endOffset n_endOffset ] 		[ ?prop l_prop ] 		;repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here 	);end first enclosure subpath list 		... 	;end of enclosure subpath lists ;end Enclosure Subpath Arguments  [ ?subRect l_subrectArgs...  ] ;start Subrectangle Arguments (l_subrectArgs) list( 	list( 		[ ?layer txl_layer ] 		[ ?width n_width ] 		[ ?length n_length ] 		[ ?choppable g_choppable ] 		[ ?sep n_sep ] 		[ ?justification S_justification ] 		[ ?space n_space ]	 		[ ?beginOffset n_beginOffset ] 		[ ?endOffset n_endOffset ] 		[ ?beginSegOffset n_beginSegOffset ] 		[ ?endSegOffset n_endSegOffset ] 		[ ?prop l_prop ] 		[ ?gap S_gap ] 		;repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here 		[ ?diagonal g_diagonalSubRect  ] 	);end first subrectangle list 		 ...		 	;end subrectangle lists   );end Subrectangle Arguments );end rodCreatePath  => R_rodObj / nil
functions.description: Creates a path consisting of one or more parts at level zero in the hierarchy on the same or on different layers from a list of points or from one or more existing objects. A path consisting of multiple parts is called a multipart path. You can use the rodCreatePath function to create one-part paths, simple multipart paths, or complex multipart paths such as guard rings, transistors, buses, and shielded paths. You can assign one or more property names and values to a multipart path.

functions.name: rodCreatePolygon
functions.syntax: rodCreatePolygon(		 [ ?name S_name ] [ ?layer txl_layer ] [ ?pts l_pts ] [ ?cvId d_cvId ] [ ?fromObj Rl_fromObj ] [ ?size txf_size ] [ ?prop l_prop ] ; ROD Connectivity Arguments for Polygons [ ?netName S_netName ] [ ?termName S_termName ] [ ?termIOType S_termIOType ] [ ?pin g_pin ] [ ?pinAccessDir tl_pinAccessDir ] [ ?pinLabel g_pinLabel ] [ ?pinLabelHeight n_pinLabelHeight ] [ ?pinLabelLayer txl_pinLabelLayer ] [ ?pinLabelFont S_pinLabelFont ] [ ?pinLabelDrafting g_pinLabelDrafting ] [ ?pinLabelOrient S_pinLabelOrient ] [ ?pinLabelOffsetPoint l_pinLabelOffsetPoint ] [ ?pinLabelJust S_pinLabelJust ] [ ?pinLabelRefHandle S_pinLabelRefHandle ] );end rodCreatePolygon => R_rodObj / nil
functions.description: Creates one polygon from a list of points or from one or more named objects. Also creates a ROD object containing information associated with the polygon, including its name and database ID. The associated ROD object is identified by a ROD object ID. The polygon is created at level zero in the hierarchy. You can assign a property name and value, or a list of property names and values, to the polygon. You can specify connectivity for the polygon by associating it with a specific terminal and net. You can also make the polygon into a pin.

functions.name: rodCreateRect
functions.syntax: rodCreateRect(	 [ ?name S_name ] [ ?layer txl_layer ] [ ?width n_width ] [ ?length n_length ] [ ?origin l_origin ] [ ?bBox l_bBox ] [ ?elementsX x_elementsX ] [ ?elementsY x_elementsY ] [ ?spaceX n_spaceX ] [ ?spaceY n_spaceY ] [ ?cvId d_cvId ] [ ?fillBBox l_fillBBox ] [ ?fromObj Rl_fromObj ] [ ?size txf_size ] [ ?prop l_prop ] [ ?returnBoolean g_returnBoolean ] 	 [rodRectConnectivityArgs... ] 	; start ROD Connectivity Arguments for Rectangles (rodRectConnectivityArgs) 	[ ?netName S_netName ] 	[ ?termName S_termName ] 	[ ?termIOType S_termIOType ] 	[ ?pin g_pin ] 	[ ?pinAccessDir tl_pinAccessDir ] 	[ ?pinLabel g_pinLabel ] 	[ ?pinLabelHeight n_pinLabelHeight ] 	[ ?pinLabelLayer txl_pinLabelLayer ] 	[ ?pinLabelFont S_pinLabelFont ] 	[ ?pinLabelDrafting g_pinLabelDrafting ] 	[ ?pinLabelOrient S_pinLabelOrient ] 	[ ?pinLabelOffsetPoint l_pinLabelOffsetPoint ] 	[ ?pinLabelJust S_pinLabelJust ] 	[ ?pinLabelRefHandle S_pinLabelRefHandle ] 	;end ROD Connectivity Arguments for Rectangles  [ ?subRectArray     l_subrectArgs... ] ;start l_subrectArgs Subrectangle Arguments (l_subrectArgs) list( 	list( 		[ ?layer txl_layer  ] 		[ ?width n_width ] 		[ ?length n_length ] 		[ ?gap S_gap ] 		[ ?lowerLeftOffsetX n_lowerLeftOffsetX ] 		[ ?lowerLeftOffsetY n_lowerLeftOffsetY ] 		[ ?upperRightOffsetX n_upperRightOffsetX ] 		[ ?upperRightOffsetY n_upperRightOffsetY ] 		[ ?spaceX n_spaceX ] 		[ ?spaceY n_spaceY ] 		[ ?prop l_prop ] 	;Repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here 	);end first subrectangle list 	...		 	) ;end all subrectangle lists ;end l_subrectArgs );end rodCreateRect  => R_rodObj | t / nil
functions.description: Creates a single named rectangle, one or more rows and/or columns of named rectangles, or fills a bounding box with named rectangles, where each rectangle has ROD attributes. You can create these named rectangles with the arguments S_name through g_returnBoolean. Each named rectangle is a separate object, created at level zero in the hierarchy. You can also create multipart rectangles by specifying one or more arrays of unnamed subrectangles for each named rectangle, where each unnamed subrectangle is an ordinary database shape, with no ROD attributes, created at level zero in the hierarchy. The named rectangles in a multipart rectangle are referred to as master rectangles.

functions.name: rodDeleteHandle
functions.syntax: rodDeleteHandle(	 R_rodObj S_name );end rodDeleteHandle => t / nil
functions.description: Deletes a user-defined handle. You provide the ROD object ID and handle name.

functions.name: rodDeleteSubPart
functions.syntax: rodDeleteSubPart(	 R_rodObjId t_subpartName );end rodDeleteSubPart => t / nil
functions.description: Deletes the named subpart from the given multipart path (MPP).

functions.name: rodFillBBoxWithRects
functions.syntax: rodFillBBoxWithRects(	 [ ?cvId d_cvId ] [ ?layer txl_layer ] [ ?fillBBox l_fillBBox ] [ ?width n_width ] [ ?length n_length ] [ ?gap S_gap ] [ ?spaceX n_spaceX ] [ ?spaceY n_spaceY ] [ ?prop l_prop ] [ ?returnBoolean g_returnBoolean ] );end rodFillBBoxWithRects => d_dbId / t / nil
functions.description: Fills a bounding box with rectangles, as many as fit within the bounding box you specify. The rectangles are ordinary unnamed shapes, identified by database IDs; the rectangles have no ROD attributes. You can assign a property name and value, or a list of property names and values, to the set of rectangles. The property or list of properties apply to every rectangle in the bounding box. You specify the return value of the function to be Boolean or a list of the database IDs for the rectangles. When you want to create a one- or two-dimensional array of rectangles, and the rectangles do not need to be ROD objects, use this function instead of rodCreateRect because regular database shapes require less overhead, contributing to faster performance.

functions.name: rodFillWithRects
functions.syntax: rodFillWithRects( [ ?shapeId d_shapeID ] [ ?fillShapeLPP lpp ] [ ?fillShapeWidth n_width ] [ ?fillShapeLength n_length ] [ ?gap S_gap ] [ ?justification S_justification ] [ ?keepOut l_ptList ] [ ?spaceX n_spaceX ] [ ?spaceY n_spaceY ] [ ?enclosureX n_encX ] [ ?enclosureY n_encY ] [ ?grid n_grid ] [ ?outputFillShape l_dbId ] );end rodFillWithRects => t / nil
functions.description: Fills a base shape with rectangles. The base shape can be a rectangle, polygon or a path type.

functions.name: rodForceUpdate
functions.description: Applies all ROD update requests in the queue.

functions.name: rodGetBBox
functions.syntax: rodGetBBox(	 [ ?figId d_figId ] [ ?layer t_layer ] [ ?purpose t_purpose ] [ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ] [ ?filterText g_filterText ] );end rodGetBBox => l_bBox / nil
functions.description: Returns the coordinates of the rectangular bounding box enclosing all the elements of a specified figure on a specified layer. You can optionally limit the calculation to include only elements on a specified layer purpose and down to a specified level of design hierarchy. You can also exclude labels and text displays from the calculation.

functions.name: rodGetHandle
functions.syntax: rodGetHandle(	 R_rodObj S_name );end rodGetHandle => g_handleValue / nil
functions.description: Returns the value of a system- or user-defined handle. You specify the handle name and the ROD object ID for the object with which the handle is associated.

functions.name: rodGetNamedShapes
functions.description: Returns a list of the ROD object IDs for all named shapes (rectangles, polygons, and paths) at level zero in the hierarchy within the specified cellview that are ROD objects. This function looks only at the top level of hierarchy and does not return the ROD object ID for instances or cellviews.

functions.name: rodGetObj
functions.syntax: rodGetObj(	 S_hierarchicalName | d_dbId [d_cellViewId] ); end rodGetObj => R_rodObj / nil
functions.description: Lets you find a named object at any level of hierarchy in your cellview. You must specify either the database ID for the object or its hierarchical name. If you specify the hierarchical name, you must also specify the cellview ID. When you specify a cellview ID, it is not necessary to also specify the database ID; however, if you specify both, the cellview ID must be correct for the database ID you specify. If your rodGetObj statement occurs in the code for a Pcell (in the body of a pcDefinePCell function or tcCreateCDSDeviceClass function call), specifying the cellview ID is optional; if you do not specify it, the cellview ID defaults to pcCellView or tcCellView, respectively.

functions.name: rodGetSubPart
functions.syntax: rodGetSubPart(	 R_rodObjId t_subpartName );end rodGetSubPart => R_rodSubpartId / nil
functions.description: Returns the subpart ID corresponding to the specified subpart name for the multipart path (MPP) specified as rodObjectId.

functions.name: rodIsFigNameUnused
functions.description: Determines whether the name specified by S_name is a valid name and whether it is already assigned to a ROD object, instance, or mosaic in the cellview specified by d_cvId. A valid name cannot contain hierarchy (indicated by one or more slashes) and cannot be an empty string.

functions.name: rodIsHandle
functions.syntax: rodIsHandle(	 R_rodObj S_name );end rodIsHandle => t / nil
functions.description: Determines whether the name specified for S_name identifies a valid system- or user-defined handle associated with the object specified by R_rodObj. Use this function prior to the rodGetHandle function when you want to verify that the handle exists before you try to access it.

functions.name: rodIsMasterChoppable
functions.description: Returns the value of the MPP master path choppability attribute.

functions.name: rodIsObj
functions.description: Determines whether the object specified for g_object identifies a valid ROD object. This function is useful for testing variables and parameters to see if they contain a ROD object ID.

functions.name: rodNameObject
functions.syntax: rodNameObject	( [ ?name S_name ] [ ?shapeId d_shapeId ] [ ?permitRename g_permitRename ] );end rodNameObject => R_rodObj / nil
functions.description: Assigns a name to an unnamed database shape or renames a ROD shape. Once the object is named, it can identified by a ROD object ID. This is an alias to an existing public function, rodNameShape.

functions.name: rodNameShape
functions.syntax: rodNameShape(	 [ ?name S_name ] [ ?shapeId d_shapeId ] [ ?permitRename g_permitRename ] );end rodNameShape => R_rodObj / nil
functions.description: Assigns a name to an unnamed database shape or renames a ROD shape. Creates (or updates) a ROD object containing information associated with the shape, including its name and database ID. The associated ROD object is identified by a ROD object ID. Optionally, you can specify whether to rename an existing ROD object.

functions.name: rodPointX
functions.description: Returns the X coordinate of the point specified by l_point.

functions.name: rodPointY
functions.description: Returns the Y coordinate of the point specified by l_point.

functions.name: rodSetMasterChoppable
functions.syntax: rodSetMasterChoppable( R_rodObjId g_setting { t | nil } ) => t / nil
functions.description: Sets the choppability attribute of an MPP master path to the specified value.

functions.name: rodSubPoints
functions.syntax: rodSubPoints( l_point1	 l_point2 ) ;end rodSubPoints => l_point / nil
functions.description: Subtracts l_point2 from l_point1 and returns the resulting point as l_point.

functions.name: rodUnAlign
functions.description: When you specify only one ROD object ID, removes all alignments for the object specified. When you specify two ROD object IDs, removes only the alignment between the two objects.

functions.name: rodUnNameShape
functions.description: Removes the name from a named shape or list of named shapes. The ROD object ID for the shape and all user-defined handles associated with it are deleted. If the object is an instance, the instance keeps its name but all user-defined handles associated with the instance are deleted. Also removes all alignment constraints that reference the shape.

functions.name: absAbstract
functions.description: Runs the Abstract step for selected cells and creates an abstract view for those cells based on the options set using absSetBinOption.

functions.name: absAttachTechLib
functions.description: Attaches the named technology library to the current library.

functions.name: absCopyBinOptions
functions.syntax: absCopyBinOptions( from_bin { Core | IO | Corner | Block | Ignore | user_bin_name } to_bin { Core | IO | Corner | Block | Ignore | user_bin_name } ) => t / nil
functions.description: Copies bin option settings from one bin to another.

functions.name: absDeleteBin
functions.description: Deletes the named user bin. You cannot delete a system bin.

functions.name: absDeleteBinMoveCellsTo
functions.syntax: absDeleteBinMoveCellsTo( name { Core | IO | Corner | Block | Ignore | user_bin_name } ) => t / nil
functions.description: Deletes a named user bin and moves any cells in that bin to another specified bin.

functions.name: absDeselectAllBins
functions.description: Deselects all currently selected bins.

functions.name: absDeselectBin
functions.description: Deselects a named bin.

functions.name: absDeselectBinFrom
functions.description: Deselects a range of bins. The deselection is done from top to bottom starting from the from bin. The from bin should be above the to bin the Bin pane, otherwise all bins listed after from are deselected.

functions.name: absDeselectCell
functions.description: Deselects a named cell.

functions.name: absDeselectCellFrom
functions.description: Deselects a range of cells. The deselection is done from top to bottom starting from the from cell. The from cell should be above the to cell the Cell pane, otherwise all cells listed after from are deselected.

functions.name: absDeselectCells
functions.description: Deselects all cells in the current bins.

functions.name: absDeselectCellsInList
functions.description: Deselects a list of cells that are not adjacent to each other in the Cell pane.

functions.name: absDisableUpdate
functions.description: Both the absDisableUpdate and absEnableUpdate functions are used to control whether or not the graphical user interface updates in response to changes in, for example, bin selection. This ensures that the GUI does not update unnecessarily when several events in a row are processed. This is inserted by Abstract Generator into the record file.

functions.name: absDistributeCells
functions.description: Distributes cells between bins according to the options set.

functions.name: absEnableUpdate
functions.description: Both the absEnableUpdate and absDisableUpdate functions are used to control whether or not the graphical user interface updates in response to changes in, for example, bin selection. This ensures that the GUI does not update unnecessarily when several events in a row are processed. This is inserted by Abstract Generator into the record file.

functions.name: absExit
functions.description: Closes Abstract Generator.

functions.name: absExportLEF
functions.description: Generates LEF files for cells in one or more bins. All exported LEF data is contained in the LEF filename.

functions.name: absExportOptions
functions.description: Save the options settings for the current session to a specified location.

functions.name: absExportReport
functions.description: Outputs a summary of the cells in your library to a report file.

functions.name: absExtract
functions.description: Runs connectivity extraction for the selected cells and creates an extracted view for these cells based on the options set using absSetBinOption.

functions.name: absGetBinOption
functions.description: Returns the value of a specified option in a given bin.

functions.name: absGetBinType
functions.description: Returns the type of the bin passed as an argument. Both system and user bins can be specified as arguments.

functions.name: absGetBins
functions.description: Displays the list of available bins. The list returned includes the five system bins as well as the user bins, if any.

functions.name: absGetCellProp
functions.description: Returns the specified property value for a cell.

functions.name: absGetLibrary
functions.description: Returns the name of the current library.

functions.name: absGetOption
functions.description: Returns the value of the specified global option.

functions.name: absGetSelectedBins
functions.description: Returns the list of bins selected in the Bin pane. The order of the bins in the list matches the order in which they appear in the Bin pane.

functions.name: absGetSelectedCells
functions.description: Returns the list of cells selected in the Cell pane. The cells might belong to different bins.

functions.name: absGetTerminalProp
functions.syntax: absGetTerminalProp( cell terminal property { direction | termType | shape | netExpr | suppSensitivity | groundSensitivity } ) => string
functions.description: Returns the value of the specified property for the specified terminal. Specify only cells that have already been processed by absPins. The Pins step generates the cell terminals.

functions.name: absImportCTLF
functions.description: Creates cellviews from CTLF logical data.

functions.name: absImportDEF
functions.description: Creates cellviews from DEF data.

functions.name: absImportGDS
functions.description: Creates cellviews from GDSII layout data.

functions.name: absImportLEF
functions.description: Creates cellviews from LEF data.

functions.name: absImportLogical
functions.description: Creates cellviews from existing logical information, typically represented in LIB or Verilog formats.

functions.name: absImportOasis
functions.description: Creates cellviews from OASIS data.

functions.name: absImportOptions
functions.description: Loads a previous session's saved options file from the specified location.

functions.name: absImportVerilog
functions.description: Creates cellviews from Verilog logical data.

functions.name: absMoveSelectedCellsToBin
functions.description: Moves any currently selected cells to a named bin. This can be one of the five system bins or a user-defined bin.

functions.name: absNewBin
functions.syntax: absNewBin( name { Core | IO | Corner | Block | Ignore } ) => t / nil
functions.description: Creates a new user bin to store library cells.

functions.name: absPins
functions.description: Runs the Pins step for the selected cells and creates a pins view for those cells based on options set using absSetBinOption.

functions.name: absRenameBin
functions.description: Renames a previously created user bin.

functions.name: absRevalidateSelectedCells
functions.description: Revalidates all invalid views for cells selected in the Cell pane. If the view has an error or warning, this remains. The view status is no longer grayed out.

functions.name: absSelect
functions.description: Selects cells according to the specified options.

functions.name: absSelectAllBins
functions.description: Selects all the bins in the current library.

functions.name: absSelectBin
functions.description: Selects the named bin. This makes the specified bin current for use with other functions.

functions.name: absSelectBinFrom
functions.description: Selects a range of bins. The selection is made from top to bottom starting from the from bin. The from bin should be above the to bin the Bins pane, otherwise all bins listed after from are selected.

functions.name: absSelectCell
functions.description: Selects a single named cell.

functions.name: absSelectCellFrom
functions.description: Selects a range of cells. The selection is made from top to bottom starting from the from cell. The from cell should be above the to cell the Cell pane, otherwise all cells listed after from are selected.

functions.name: absSelectCells
functions.description: Selects all cells in the selected bins.

functions.name: absSelectCellsInList
functions.description: Selects a list of cells that are not adjacent to each other in the Cell pane.

functions.name: absSetBinOption
functions.syntax: absSetBinOption( bin option value ) => t / nil
functions.description: Sets a value for a specified option in a specified bin.

functions.name: absSetCellProp
functions.description: Specifies a property value for a cell. The variables you can use for the value parameter depend on the property.

functions.name: absSetLibrary
functions.description: Specifies the library that you want to process through Abstract Generator. This involves either creating a new library and setting into it or setting into an existing library.

functions.name: absSetOption
functions.description: Sets values for all abstract generator global options. The SKILL function to apply the absSetOption settings is run after the absSetOption function has been set.

functions.name: absSetTerminalProp
functions.syntax: absSetTerminalProp( cell terminal property { direction | termType | shape | netExpr | suppSensitivity | groundSensitivity } value ) => 0 / 1
functions.description: Specifies a terminal value for a cell. The variables you can use for the value parameter depend on the property setting.

functions.name: absSort
functions.description: Sets sort criteria for those cells in the current bin.

functions.name: absVerify
functions.description: Runs the Verify step for selected cells and creates a verify view for those cells based on the options set using absSetBinOption.

functions.name: absVersion
functions.description: Returns version, build, and operating system information.

functions.name: iagCreateMenuItem
functions.description: Creates a custom menu item with the user-specified name and adds it to the integrated Abstract Generator. The menu is created if it is not already available, and the menu item is added under it. Function name is the callback procedure for the menu item.

functions.name: iagGenAbstract
functions.syntax: iagGenAbstract( t_libName l_cellNames t_viewName t_binName t_optionsFilePath ) => t / nil
functions.description: Runs Integrated Abstract Generator on the specified cellviews with the given settings.

functions.name: annLoadAnnotationData
functions.description: Loads the saved annotation setup files into the current schematic design. You can specify multiple annotation setup files to load.

functions.name: annPinCurrentInfoBalloon
functions.description: Pins the current unpinned annotation balloon on the specified schematic window.

functions.name: annSaveAnnotationData
functions.description: Saves the current annotation setup in a file. You can specify the complete file path where the setup file needs to be saved.

functions.name: annToggleInfoBalloonVisibilityStatus
functions.description: Toggles the visibility of the annotation balloons on the schematic canvas. Also, displays and removes the pinned balloons on all open schematic windows.

functions.name: cdsName
functions.description: The cdsName function uses information about the instance currently being drawn in order to compute the data returned by the schematic editor during a redraw. Consequently, cdsName is only intended to be called as the value of an ILLabel on a symbol, and is not intended for direct evaluation during a program. If it is invoked directly, information on the current drawn instance will not be available. The cdsName will display label information, usually placed on the layer annotate drawing7, near the cell name or instance name.

functions.name: cdsNetExpr
functions.description: The cdsNetExpr function is used inside the ILLabel that is created using the Create - Net Expression command. This function uses information about the instance currently being drawn in order to compute the data returned by the schematic editor during a redraw. Consequently, cdsNetExpr is only intended to be called as the value of an ILLabel on a symbol, and is not intended for direct evaluation during a program. If it is invoked directly, information on the current drawn instance will not be available.

functions.name: cdsParam
functions.description: The cdsParam function displays label information, usually placed on the layer annotate drawing, about the parameter values or backannotated parameter values. This function uses information about the instance currently being drawn in order to compute the data returned by the schematic editor during a redraw. Consequently, cdsParam is only intended to be called as the value of an ILLabel on a symbol, and is not intended for direct evaluation during a program. If it is invoked directly, information on the current drawn instance will not be available.

functions.name: cdsTerm
functions.description: The function cdsTerm displays label information, usually placed on the layer annotate drawing8, near the pin or a net attached to the pin. It is also attached to a cell symbol view when you use the Add Symbol Label form, and the Annotation Setup Form is used to control the display of this label type.

functions.name: defcell
functions.syntax: defcell( t_cellName t_pinType t_pinName defsymbol t_viewname symbolProps t_propName g_propValue defTermProp t_defPinName defVisibleProp labelAttr symbolParam f_spacing f_length f_vLength f_hLength t_connector t_origin symbolLabels t_labelText controlParam g_boolean pinNumSpec t_pinName x_pinNumber pinLocSpec t_leftPinName t_rightPinName t_topPinName t_bottomPinName pinGraphicSpec t_pinGraph pinLogicSpec t_posPin t_negPin clockPins t_clockPin ) => t / nil
functions.description: Used with TSG template files to call lmdefcell.

functions.name: heHiEditConfig
functions.description: Opens the hierarchy editor if the current editing window has a design opened within the context of a configuration.

functions.name: heHiSetInstBinding
functions.description: Sets the instance bindings of an instance in a cellview of open configurations. The form associated with this function is updated with current binding information. The new bindings are communicated to the hierarchy editor.

functions.name: heHiShowViewsFound
functions.description: Shows the current view being used for each instance in a form.

functions.name: heHiUpdate
functions.description: Updates the information in the hierarchy editor after you edit the configuration.

functions.name: hsmDeselect
functions.syntax: hsmDeselect( [ ?type d_type ] [ ?path g_path ] [ ?name g_name ] [ ?spec l_spec ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Deselects named objects in the design hierarchy.

functions.name: hsmGetSelectedSet
functions.syntax: hsmGetSelectedSet( [ ?top g_top ] [ ?type d_type ] [ ?pathStyle g_pathStyle ] [ ?includeExtra g_includeExtra ] [ ?cellview d_cellview ] [ ?path g_path ] ) => list / nil
functions.description: Gets the hierarchical selected set.

functions.name: hsmSelect
functions.syntax: hsmSelect( [ ?type d_type ] [ ?path g_path ] [ ?name g_name ] [ ?spec l_spec ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Selects named objects in the design hierarchy.

functions.name: lmCheckTerm
functions.description: Checks the consistency of terminal name, type, and wth for all views of each specified cell.

functions.name: lmCheckView
functions.description: Evaluates a sequence of expressions for each specified cellview. Checks the property value for consistency.

functions.name: lmCloseLib
functions.description: Closes the previously opened working library.

functions.name: lmDefTermProp
functions.syntax: lmDefTermProp(  [ t_cellName ]  [ t_viewName ]  ( g_terminalList t_propertyName t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName = t_propertyValue )  ( g_terminalList t_propertyName = t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName t_propertyValue )  )
functions.description: Adds properties to the terminals of the specified cellview. To add terminal properties, add specified properties to the original property list and save the new file.

functions.name: lmDefViewProp
functions.syntax: lmDefViewProp(  [ t_cellName ]  [ t_viewName ]  ( t_propertyName t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName t_propertyValue ) )
functions.description: Adds properties to the specified cellview. To add properties, add the specified properties to the original property list and save the new file.

functions.name: lmDeleteTermProp
functions.syntax: lmDeleteTermProp(  d_cellList  t_viewName  ( g_terminalList ... t_propertyName g_terminalList ... t_propertyName )  )
functions.description: Deletes specified properties from the terminals of specified views.

functions.name: lmDeleteViewProp
functions.description: Deletes specified properties from the specified view.

functions.name: lmGetValue
functions.description: Returns the value of a specified view property in the current referenced view.

functions.name: lmLoadData
functions.syntax: lmLoadData(  t_file  t_lib [ { t_path | nil } [ { t_config | nil } [ { t_mode | nil } ] ] ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Opens a working library, loads the library command file, and closes the library when you are finished.

functions.name: lmOpenLib
functions.syntax: lmOpenLib(  t_lib [ { t_path | nil } [ { t_config | nil } [ { t_mode | nil } ] ] ]  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Opens a library.

functions.name: lmPrintLibTermProp
functions.description: Prints terminal properties of the specified view for each cell in the current library.

functions.name: lmPrintLibViewProp
functions.description: Prints properties of the specified view for each cell in the current library.

functions.name: lmPrintTerm
functions.description: Prints names, types, and wths of all terminals of the specified cellviews.

functions.name: lmPrintTermProp
functions.description: Prints properties of all terminals of the specified views of a cell.

functions.name: lmPrintViewProp
functions.description: Prints properties of all specified views of a cell.

functions.name: lmReset
functions.description: Resets all global variables to their default values.

functions.name: lmSimView
functions.syntax: lmSimView(  t_cellName  t_templateViewName  t_targetViewName  [ t_targetViewtype ] t_propertyName = t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName t_propertyValue  )
functions.description: Creates a view with specified properties for the specified cell.

functions.name: opcAddListToSet
functions.description: Adds a list of objects to the specified set.

functions.name: opcAddObjectToSet
functions.description: Adds an object to the specified set.

functions.name: opcAllSetsInCellView
functions.description: Returns a list of all the sets present in the specified cellview.

functions.name: opcClearSet
functions.description: Removes all objects from a set without modifying the specific objects.

functions.name: opcCreateCondition
functions.syntax: opcCreateCondition(  ?attrName s_attrName ?opName g_opName ?value t_value ) => nil / list
functions.description: Defines a condition to be used in Navigator custom queries.

functions.name: opcCreateExpression
functions.syntax: opcCreateExpression(  ?dataSource s_dataSource ?dataType t_dataType [ ?conditions l_conditions ] ) => nil / list
functions.description: Defines an expression to be used in Navigator custom queries.

functions.name: opcCreatePersistentSet
functions.description: Creates an OPC set that has a persistent storage in the cellview.

functions.name: opcCreateQuery
functions.syntax: opcCreateQuery(  ?name t_name [ ?category t_category ] [ ?appName t_appName ] [ ?expressions l_expressions ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Defines a query that can be instantiated in a cellview to generate a set of objects matching the expressions that constitute the Navigator custom query.

functions.name: opcCreateTransientSet
functions.description: Creates an OPC set that is deleted when the cellview is removed from memory. Such sets can be created even when the cellview is read-only.

functions.name: opcDeleteQuery
functions.description: Deletes the definition of a query along with any sets that have been created using the query.

functions.name: opcDestroySet
functions.description: Removes the set from memory and storage.

functions.name: opcEditQuery
functions.description: Edits the definition of a query in a modal popup form.

functions.name: opcFindSet
functions.description: Searches for the specified OPC set name in the given cellview.

functions.name: opcInstantiateQuery
functions.syntax: opcInstantiateQuery(  ?query t_query ?cv d_cv [ ?category t_category ] ) => t / nil
functions.description: Instantiates a query in a cellview. If a category is specified, the query is instantiated in the specified category. Otherwise, the query is instantiated in the same category as the query.

functions.name: opcLoadQueries
functions.description: Loads all the queries defined in the specified file.

functions.name: opcRefreshSet
functions.description: Refreshes the content of an operating collections set derived from a query containing SKILL customization.

functions.name: opcReleaseSet
functions.description: Removes from cache the sets contained in the specified cellview, but retains them on the hard disk. The function is intended to release memory when critical operations need to be run.

functions.name: opcRemoveObjectFromSet
functions.description: Removes an object from the specified set.

functions.name: opcSaveQueries
functions.description: Saves the list of queries in the specified file.

functions.name: schAddIgnoreProp
functions.syntax: schAddIgnoreProp(  t_name t_prompt t_type t_value g_enable ) => t / nil
functions.description: Registers an ignore property. You can view the set of registered ignore properties on the Ignore Properties tab by clicking Options - Editor in the schematic window.

functions.name: schAddSelectPt
functions.description: Selects the object under the cursor. Maintains the selected set and adds the object to the selected set. Usable when editing schematics. Is equivalent to the Graphics Editor mouseAddSelectPt function. Provides other functions with the identity of the most recently selected object, which is required for extended selection.

functions.name: schAlign
functions.description: Aligns the objects in the specified direction in the schematic or symbol view.

functions.name: schAttachLibToPackageTech
functions.description: Attaches a package technology to the given library.

functions.name: schCheck
functions.description: Performs a check on the specified cellview. This includes extracting connectivity, running the schematic rules checker, and running the cross-view checker. You must have write permission to any cellview that is to be checked. The given cellview ID can be read-only or editable schematic.

functions.name: schCheckHier
functions.syntax: schCheckHier(  d_cvId  t_viewNames  t_refLibs  [ l_instViewListTable ]  )  => l_errors / nil
functions.description: Performs a check of the hierarchy that starts at the given cellview.

functions.name: schCheckHierConfig
functions.syntax: schCheckHierConfig(  h_cfgId  [ v_pathVector [ g_refLibs ] ]  )  => l_errors / nil
functions.description: Performs a check of the hierarchy. The check starts with the top cellview that is specified in the given hierarchy configuration. The hierarchy traversed is defined by information in this hierarchy configuration. Usually, the hierarchy is confined to the library of the given cellview, but you can specify a list of reference libraries to process if the hierarchy extends beyond the current library.

functions.name: schClearConn
functions.description: Removes the schematic connectivity from a specified cellview to restart extraction using schExtractConn.

functions.name: schCloneSymbol
functions.syntax: schCloneSymbol(  d_cvId  d_masterId  l_origin  t_orient  )  => t / nil
functions.description: Copies or clones graphics from an existing symbol into the target symbol cellview with the given location and orientation.

functions.name: schCmdOption
functions.description: Cycles through a predefined set of values. By default, this function is bound to the middle mouse button. When you click the right mouse button during an active command, the command applies the next value in the predefined set.

functions.name: schComputePinRef
functions.syntax: schComputePinRef(  d_cellView  [ ?reportFile t_reportFile ]  [ ?display t_display ]  [ ?formatString t_formatString ]  [ ?reportDups t_reportDups ]  [ ?sortByDir t_sortByDir ]  [ ?separator t_separator ]  [ ?inputDesignator t_inputDesignator ]  [ ?outputDesignator t_outputDesignator ]  [ ?ioDesignator t_ioDesignator ]  [ ?charsPerLine x_charsPerLine ]  ) => t / nil
functions.description: Creates offsheet pin references for multisheet designs. The pin references can be displayed in the schematic next to each pin or in a report file. This function creates an offsheet pin reference report that lists each pin followed by a list of all other locations of this pin. The pin references can also be displayed in the schematic next to each pin.

functions.name: schCopy
functions.syntax: schCopy(  d_fig  d_destCV  l_transform  ) => d_object / nil
functions.description: Copies the given object to the given destination cellview. The object location and orientation can be specified before it is placed at the destination location by the given transformation argument. The copied figure is first rotated and reflected about the origin as specified by the orientation of the transform, then translated by the offset of the transform.

functions.name: schCreateInst
functions.syntax: schCreateInst(  d_cvId  d_masterId  t_instanceName  l_origin  t_orient  [ n_magnification ]  ) => d_inst / nil
functions.description: Creates an instance of the given master cellview in the specified cellview at the given location with the given orientation. You can specify the magnification to set for the instance. Although not fully supported, you can use this property to scale the appearance of an instance.

functions.name: schCreateInstBox
functions.description: Creates an instance box in the given symbol cellview. This function uses a bounding box you specify or determines a bounding box from the pins and device shapes.

functions.name: schCreateNetExpression
functions.syntax: schCreateNetExpression(  d_cvId  t_netExpr  d_glueId  l_point  t_justify  t_orient  t_fontStyle  n_fontHeight  ) => d_id / nil
functions.description: Creates an inherited connection and the corresponding net expression label. Attaches the given net expression to the given database object. It validates the syntax of the expression and attaches a net expression label to the database object. If the object is a schematic wire, you must run the schematic extractor to create the inherited connection. Before calling this function, you must acquire all the required arguments of the function.

functions.name: schCreateNoteLabel
functions.syntax: schCreateNoteLabel(  d_cvId  l_point  t_text  t_just  t_orient  t_fontStyle  n_fontHeight  t_type  ) => d_label / nil
functions.description: Creates note labels in a schematic or symbol cellview with the attributes and properties you specify. These labels do not affect the connectivity but can be useful for annotation.

functions.name: schCreateNoteShape
functions.syntax: schCreateNoteShape(  d_cvId  t_type  t_lineStyle  l_points  [ n_width ]  ) => d_shape / nil
functions.description: Creates note shapes in a schematic or symbol cellview with the attributes and properties you specify. These shapes do not affect the connectivity but can be useful for annotation.

functions.name: schCreatePin
functions.syntax: schCreatePin(  d_cvId  d_master  t_termName  t_direction  g_offSheetP  l_origin  t_orientation [ g_powerSens ] [ g_groundSens ] [ g_sigType ] ) => d_pin / nil
functions.description: Creates instances that are used to represent pins of terminals in a schematic cellview. Creates only a pin in a schematic cellview. The destination cellview must not be the same as the master cellview and must be editable.

functions.name: schCreateSheet
functions.syntax: schCreateSheet(  d_cvId  x_number  t_borderLibrary  t_borderCell  t_borderView  ) => d_sheetInstId / nil
functions.description: Creates a new sheet for a multisheet schematic.

functions.name: schCreateSplitPrimarySymbol
functions.description: Searches for split symbol views within the given cell and creates a split-primary symbol by assembling all the terminals from the gathered views. The generated split-primary cellview has the view name as symbol. This function removes an existing split-primary cellview, if any, and replaces it with a new one.

functions.name: schCreateSymbolLabel
functions.syntax: schCreateSymbolLabel(  d_cvId  l_point  t_labelChoice  t_text  t_justify  t_orient  t_fontStyle  n_fontHeight  t_type  ) => d_label / nil
functions.description: Creates a label in only a symbol cellview with the specified attributes that is opened in append mode.

functions.name: schCreateSymbolPin
functions.syntax: schCreateSymbolPin(  d_cvId  d_master  t_termName  t_direction  l_origin  t_orientation  [ g_flatten ] [g_powerSens] [g_groundSens] [g_sigType] ) => t_pinFigId / nil
functions.description: Creates a pin in the given cellview with the name, direction, and orientation you specify.

functions.name: schCreateSymbolShape
functions.syntax: schCreateSymbolShape(  d_cvId  t_shape  t_style  l_points  [ n_width ]  ) => d_shapeId / nil
functions.description: Creates the specified shape using the given fill style and the list of points in the given cellview.

functions.name: schCreateWire
functions.syntax: schCreateWire(  d_cvId  t_entryMethod  t_routeMethod  l_points  n_xSpacing  n_ySpacing  n_width  [ t_color ] [ t_lineStyle ] ) => l_wireId
functions.description: Creates flight lines, wide wires, or narrow wires in the specified schematic cellview.

functions.name: schCreateWireLabel
functions.syntax: schCreateWireLabel(  d_cvId  d_glue  l_point  t_text  t_justify  t_orient  t_fontStyle  n_fontHeight  g_aliasP  ) => d_labelId / nil
functions.description: Creates wire labels and glues them to the object you specify.

functions.name: schDelete
functions.description: Deletes the figure or object you specify only from schematic or symbol cellviews.

functions.name: schDeleteIndex
functions.description: Deletes an index schematic if there is one remaining sheet. Converts the remaining sheet into an ordinary schematic with the cell name of the index schematic and replaces any offsheet pins with schematic pins.

functions.name: schDeleteSheet
functions.description: Deletes a sheet from a multisheet schematic design.

functions.name: schDeselectAllFig
functions.description: Deselects all objects in a specified cellview. Bypasses the selection filter.

functions.name: schDirectEdit
functions.description: Directly edits or manipulates the object under the cursor. Usable when editing schematics and symbols.

functions.name: schDistribute
functions.description: Arranges objects at equal distance in the specified direction in the schematic or symbol view.

functions.name: schDrawSymbolPin
functions.syntax: schDrawSymbolPin(  d_cvId  t_termName  t_direction  l_points  ) => t_pinFigId / nil
functions.description: Creates a symbol pin in the specified cellview by creating a terminal of the given name with the given direction and a polygon shape specified by the given list of points.

functions.name: schEditPinOrder
functions.syntax: schEditPinOrder(  d_cvId  l_pinList  g_updateInstLastChanged  ) => t / nil
functions.description: Updates the pin ordering for schematic or symbol cellviews given a list of pin names contained in the cellview and their desired order.

functions.name: schEditSheetSize
functions.syntax: schEditSheetSize(  d_cvId  t_borderLib  t_borderCell  t_borderView  ) => t / nil
functions.description: Places or replaces a sheet border instance in a schematic. This function works for both multisheet and non-multisheet schematics.

functions.name: schExportSVG
functions.syntax: schExportSVG(  d_cellview  ?path s_path ?background s_background ?grid s_grid ?stipple s_stipple ?drawBBox g_drawBBox ?nameCallback g_nameCallback ) => t / nil
functions.description: Exports a schematic as a vector image in SVG format.

functions.name: schExtendSelSet
functions.description: Extends the selection of the object in the specified position by selecting the object around the current object.

functions.name: schExtendSelectPt
functions.description: Extends the selection of the object under the current cursor position by selecting objects around the current object. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schExtractConn
functions.description: Runs the schematic connectivity extractor on the cellview you specify.

functions.name: schExtractStatus
functions.description: Checks for error and warning markers before returning the schematic extraction status for the specified schematic cellview. When the schematic is read-only, schExtractStatus() will also check whether any instance masters have been updated since the schematic was last saved.

functions.name: schFindIgnorePropByName
functions.description: Searches for an ignore property in the registered property set. You can view the registered ignore property set by clicking Options - Editor - Ignore Properties tab in the schematic window.

functions.name: schGetAllIgnoreProps
functions.description: Returns a disembodied property list for all the ignore properties that are currently registered. You can view the set of registered ignore properties set on the Ignore Properties tab by clicking Options - Editor in the schematic window.

functions.name: schGetBundleDisplayMode
functions.description: Takes a label Id and returns its display mode. This only works for label type objects. If the specified object Id is not a label object, then the API will return nil. This will only work when the cellview is editable.

functions.name: schGetCellViewListInSearchScope
functions.syntax: schGetCellViewListInSearchScope(  d_cvId  t_scope  d_topCV  t_viewNameList  t_libName  t_mode  ) => l_cvList / nil
functions.description: Returns a list of cellviews in the search scope you specify. Only cellviews of the same view type as the base cellview are returned.

functions.name: schGetCheckGroups
functions.description: Returns an association list of all the custom schematic checker groups created using schRegisterCheckGroup().

functions.name: schGetEnv
functions.description: Gets the value of a schematic environment variable.

functions.name: schGetIgnoredStatus
functions.description: Returns the ignored status of the given instance ID. This function can be used only when the instance IDs are known.

functions.name: schGetMatchingObjects
functions.syntax: schGetMatchingObjects(  d_cvId  t_propName  t_condOp  t_propValue  g_useSelSet  ) => l_objects / nil
functions.description: Finds the set of objects that match the specified search criteria in a cellview. You can search by property to limit the search in the selected set.

functions.name: schGetPinOrder
functions.description: Returns the pin list, as defined in the portOrder property (if present) or as the default pin list.

functions.name: schGetPostCheckTriggers
functions.description: Lists all the post-check triggers registered using schRegPostCheckTrigger.

functions.name: schGetPreCheckTriggers
functions.description: Lists all the pre-check triggers registered using schRegPreCheckTrigger.

functions.name: schGetPropertyDisplay
functions.syntax: schGetPropertyDisplay(  ?object d_object [?name S_name] ) => l_textDisplays / s_visibility / nil
functions.description: Returns the attribute, property, and parameter textDisplays enabled for an object.

functions.name: schGetShapeStyle
functions.description: Returns a Disembodied property list (DPL) containing the style attributes of a given shape.

functions.name: schGetSignalTypeIntegrity
functions.syntax: schGetSignalTypeIntegrity(  t_netSigType t_termNetSigType t_termDirection ) => t_severity / nil
functions.description: Gets the conflict severity for signal type integrity check for connections between nets of specified signal type, and instance pins of specified signal type and direction.

functions.name: schGetSplitInstTerms
functions.description: Returns a list of split instance terminals that have the same name as that of the given split-primary instance.

functions.name: schGetSplitInstances
functions.description: Returns a list of split instance IDs that are associated with the given split-primary instance.

functions.name: schGetSplitPrimaryInst
functions.description: Returns the split-primary instance associated with the given split symbol.

functions.name: schGetSplitPrimaryInstTerm
functions.description: Returns the terminal of the split-primary instance that has the same terminal name as the specified split instance terminal.

functions.name: schGetWireColor
functions.description: Returns the color used to draw a wire segment.

functions.name: schGetWireLineStyle
functions.description: Returns the line style used to draw a wire segment.

functions.name: schGlueLabel
functions.description: Glues the label to the figure you specify using a database child/parent relationship in which the label is the child. You can glue a pin label to a pin only when the label defines the name for that pin. You can glue a wire label only to a wire, a pin of a component, or a pin of a schematic. The label defines the name of the net associated with the wire, the pin of the component, or the pin of the schematic. You can glue note labels to any object.

functions.name: schHDLReturn
functions.description: Returns up the hierarchy from a Verilog view window.

functions.name: schHdlPrintFile
functions.description: Prints the current HDL file.

functions.name: schHdlPrintVars
functions.description: Prints the current values of the schematic HDL variables.

functions.name: schHiAbout
functions.description: Opens the product information window, which indicates the schematic editor release number and copyright information.

functions.name: schHiAlign
functions.description: Aligns the objects on the canvas. If the objects are already selected on the canvas, the pre-select mode is used; otherwise, the post-select mode is used for aligning the objects.

functions.name: schHiAlternateView
functions.description: Changes the view name of a single component by toggling through the list of possible views. Usable only while editing a schematic cellview. Operates on one instance at a time.

functions.name: schHiCellViewProperty
functions.description: Displays the options form showing the properties for the current cellview. Usable only when editing schematic or symbol cellviews.

functions.name: schHiChangeEditMode
functions.description: Sets the mode for the design in the current window to read or append. The mode is the same as that supplied to dbOpenCellViewByType.

functions.name: schHiCheck
functions.description: Checks the connectivity of a schematic and optionally starts the schematic rules checker (SRC) or the cross-view checker (VIC). Usable only when editing schematics. A dialog box shows the total number of errors and warnings detected when the function is complete. The schematic can be read-only or editable.

functions.name: schHiCheckAndSave
functions.description: Performs the checks specified by the check options and saves the schematic to disk under the same cell name and view name, and in the same library. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCheckHier
functions.description: Performs the specified checks on the current schematic and the hierarchy below it. Also updates the connectivity as needed and runs the schematic rules checker (SRC), the cross-view checker (VIC), or both. Usable only when editing schematics. Only processes schematics found in the hierarchy starting from the current cellview. The view name list used to control the traversal is taken from the window in which the function is run.

functions.name: schHiCloneSymbol
functions.description: Copies graphics from an existing symbol library into the symbol design you are currently editing. Usable only when editing symbols. If you do not specify any argument, the options form appears and prompts you for the values of these fields.

functions.name: schHiComputePinRef
functions.syntax: schHiComputePinRef(  [ ?reportFile t_reportFile ]  [ ?display t_display ]  [ ?formatString t_formatString ] [ ?reportDups t_reportDups ]  [ ?sortByDir t_sortByDir ]  ) => t
functions.description: Displays the Cross-Reference Options form for current index or sheet schematic, which computes, stores, and lists zone references for all pins and offsheet connectors in a multisheet schematic. The zone references identify where pins on other sheets reference the same net. Uses stored references to identify pin locations. The pin references can be displayed in the schematic alongside each pin or written to a report file. Can be used only when editing either the index or a sheet of a multisheet design. The index requires checking before zones can be computed.

functions.name: schHiCopy
functions.syntax: schHiCopy(  [ ?formFlag g_formFlag ] [ ?rows x_numrows ] [ ?columns x_numcols ] [ ?useSelSet t_useSelSet ]  ) => t
functions.description: Copies objects and data such as object properties. Objects can be copied between different schematic cellviews. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateBlockInst
functions.syntax: schHiCreateBlockInst(  [ ?libraryName t_libraryName ] [ ?cellName t_cellName ] [ ?viewName t_viewName ] [ ?blockSampleName t_blockSampleName ]  [ ?instanceName t_instanceName ] [ ?pinNameSeed t_pinNameSeed ]  ) => t
functions.description: Creates a block and places an instance of a block in a schematic. Usable only when editing schematics. If you do not type a library, cell, view, and instance name as arguments, the options form appears and prompts you for these values. The block choices are defined by the schBlockTemplate variable in the schConfig.il file. If you type freeform, the schematic editor prompts you to type a rectangular shape by clicking on two points of the rectangle.

functions.name: schHiCreateInst
functions.syntax: schHiCreateInst( [ ?libraryName t_libraryName ] [ ?cellName t_cellName ] [ ?viewName t_viewName ] [ ?instanceName t_instanceName ] [ ?rows x_rows ] [ ?columns x_columns ]  ) => t
functions.description: Places an instance of a cellview in a schematic. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCreateInstBox
functions.description: Creates an instance box for the symbol you are editing. An instance box defines a rectangular region in which an instance of a symbol is selectable. Usable only when editing symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateKanjiSymbol
functions.syntax: schHiCreateKanjiSymbol( [ ?kanjiFile t_kanjiFile ] [ ?libName t_libName ] [ ?cellName t_cellName ] [ ?viewName t_viewName ]  ) => t / nil
functions.description: Creates a symbol view containing kanji characters based on the information in an EUC-packed format kanji file. The software generates a symbol cellview that contains kanji character graphics.

functions.name: schHiCreateMappingSchematic
functions.description: Displays the Create a Mapping Schematic form.

functions.name: schHiCreateNetExpression
functions.syntax: schHiCreateNetExpression(  [ ?netExpr t_netExpr ] [ ?justify t_justify ] [ ?fontStyle t_fontStyle ] [ ?fontHeight n_fontHeight ] ) => t
functions.description: Creates an inherited connection and the corresponding net expression label. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateNoteLabel
functions.syntax: schHiCreateNoteLabel(  [ ?text t_text ] [ ?justify t_justify ] [ ?fontStyle t_fontStyle ] [ ?fontHeight n_fontHeight ] [ ?type t_type ]  ) => t
functions.description: Creates a note label to annotate the design for documentation purposes. These shapes do not affect connectivity. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateNoteShape
functions.description: Creates a shape to annotate the design for documentation purposes. These shapes do not affect connectivity. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreatePatchcord
functions.description: Displays the Create Patchcord form where you can create, and add, a patchCord instance on a schematic along with appropriately named net stubs.

functions.name: schHiCreatePin
functions.syntax: schHiCreatePin( [ ?terminalName t_terminalName ] [ ?direction t_direction ] [ ?usage t_usage ] [ ?interpret t_interpret ] [ ?mode t_mode ]  [ ?netExpr t_netExpr ] [ t_justify ] [ t_fontStyle ] [ n_fontHeight ] ) => t
functions.description: Creates a pin of a specified type in your schematic. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCreateSheet
functions.description: Creates a sheet for a multisheet schematic. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCreateSymbolLabel
functions.syntax: schHiCreateSymbolLabel( [ ?labelChoice t_labelChoice ] [ ?text t_text ] [ ?justify t_justify ] [ ?fontStyle t_fontStyle ] [ ?fontHeight n_fontHeight ] [ ?type t_type ] ) => t
functions.description: Places labels in a symbol. Usable only when editing symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateSymbolPin
functions.syntax: schHiCreateSymbolPin( [ ?terminalName t_terminalName ] [ ?type t_type ] [ ?direction t_direction ] [ ?interpret t_interpret ] [ ?mode t_mode ] [ ?incrCount n_incrCount ] [ ?location t_location ] ) => t
functions.description: Creates pins in a symbol. Usable only when editing symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateSymbolShape
functions.syntax: schHiCreateSymbolShape( [ ?shape t_shape ] [ ?style t_style ] [ ?width x_width ] [ ?nonModal g_nonModal ] ) => t
functions.description: Creates a line or shapes that describe a symbol. Usable only when editing symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateWire
functions.syntax: schHiCreateWire( [ ?width n_width ] [ ?drawMode g_drawMode ] [ ?routeMethod t_routeMethod ] [ ?lockAngle t_lockAngle ] [ ?nonModal g_nonModal ] [ ?color t_color ] [ ?lineStyle t_lineStyle ] ) => t
functions.description: Creates different style wires that represent net connections in a schematic. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCreateWireLabel
functions.syntax: schHiCreateWireLabel( [ ?text t_text ] [ ?purpose t_purpose ] [ ?justify t_justify ] [ ?fontStyle t_fontStyle ] [ ?fontHeight n_fontHeight ] [ ?interpret t_interpret ] [ ?mode t_mode ] [ ?netExprFlag g_netExprFlag ] [ ?bundleDisplay t_bundleDisplay ] ) => t
functions.description: Creates wire labels in a schematic. Physical contact between a label and wire is not required. You can move a label independently from a wire. When you move a wire that has a label glued to it, the label also moves. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCreateWireStubs
functions.description: Starts the Create Wire Stubs and Names command.

functions.name: schHiDefaultAction
functions.description: Performs the default editing action for the object under the cursor.

functions.name: schHiDelete
functions.description: Deletes selected objects. Usable when editing schematics or symbols. This function cannot be used to delete a sheet border (use schHiEditSheetSize).

functions.name: schHiDeleteIndex
functions.description: Converts a multisheet schematic having one drawing sheet and one index sheet into a single-sheet schematic. Usable only when editing an index schematic. Use schHiDeleteSheet to first remove extra drawing sheets. The index schematic must contain only one sheet.

functions.name: schHiDeleteSheet
functions.description: Deletes a sheet or range of sheets from a multisheet schematic. Usable only when editing an index of a multisheet schematic. This function cannot be undone.

functions.name: schHiDescend
functions.description: Traverses down the hierarchy and displays the child cellview of a specified instance and view you select, provided you have edit permission. If you do not have edit permission, a dialog box prompts you to use read mode.

functions.name: schHiDescendEdit
functions.description: Traverses down the hierarchy and displays the child cellview of a specified instance and view you select, provided you have edit permission. If you do not have edit permission, a dialog box prompts you to use read mode.

functions.name: schHiDescendRead
functions.description: Traverses down the hierarchy and displays the child cellview in read mode of a specified instance and view you select. The cellview is not editable.

functions.name: schHiDisplayOptions
functions.description: Sets options associated with the window display. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiDistribute
functions.description: Arranges the objects on the canvas at equal distance from each other. If the objects are already selected on the canvas, the pre-select mode is used; otherwise, the post-select mode is used for distributing the objects.

functions.name: schHiDrawSymbolPin
functions.description: Draws a polygon that represents a symbol pin. Usable only when editing symbols.

functions.name: schHiEditInPlace
functions.description: Edits the master of a user-selected instance within the context of its parent schematic. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiEditPinOrder
functions.description: Creates or modifies the property on the cellview that specifies the ordering of the pins in the current cellview. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiEditSheetSize
functions.description: Edits the sheet border size of a schematic. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiEditText
functions.description: Starts the direct text edit command in the current window, allowing you to perform an in-place edit of notes, names, parameters, and so on.

functions.name: schHiEditTitleBlock
functions.description: Changes the properties of a title block in a schematic sheet. Usable only when editing schematics that have a sheet border.

functions.name: schHiEditorOptions
functions.description: Sets variables that affect the environment. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiEnvSaveLoad
functions.description: Saves or loads the schematic environment variables. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiEscape
functions.description: Closes an open form or clears the current canvas selection. You would typically use this function to successively close the open forms on your desktop, even if they are hidden behind other windows. If there is only one form open, it is closed. If there are multiple forms open, the first form returned by the hiGetCurrentForm SKILL API is closed. If there are no forms open, the current canvas selection is cleared.

functions.name: schHiExtractConn
functions.description: Sets extraction options and runs the schematic extractor. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiFind
functions.description: Finds objects that match specified search criteria in a schematic or symbol view. You can specify the object filter as well as a property name or value expression that matches the objects. Usable when editing schematics or symbols. Matching is supported only for strings, integers, floating-point numbers, and time. Other property types are not supported.

functions.name: schHiFindMarker
functions.description: Searches for the error and warning markers generated by the schematic rules checker (SRC) and displays a form that contains a list of the markers. Usable when editing a schematic or a symbol.

functions.name: schHiFlatten
functions.description: Starts the schematic Flatten command. Flattening brings the contents of the flattened instance up to the current level to allow editing while preserving the connectivity of the flattened instance. If no single, valid instance is pre-selected, it prompts you to select an instance to flatten. When a valid instance is selected, it prompts you to select a point to place the flattened content. In the case of schematic-in-schematic, the flattened content is placed immediately, without prompting for an additional point.

functions.name: schHiFollowPin
functions.description: Changes the cellview to one that contains the specified pin or offsheet connector. Operates on the selected set. Brings in the cellview that contains the first reference of the selected pin or offsheet connector. Usable only when editing a sheet of a multisheet schematic.

functions.name: schHiFontUpdate
functions.description: Interactive command for updating the font size of text on a schematic.

functions.name: schHiGotoSheet
functions.description: Traverses sheets in a multisheet schematic. Usable only when editing an index or sheet of a multisheet schematic.

functions.name: schHiGridOptions
functions.description: Sets options associated with the grid.

functions.name: schHiHiliteLabel
functions.description: Highlights labels of wires and instances. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiIgnore
functions.description: Ignores the instances in the schematic canvas. This function works as a toggle switch, that is, it is used for adding ignore properties to an instance or for removing any existing ones. When the instances are already selected on the canvas, the pre-select mode is used; otherwise, the post-select mode is used for ignoring the instances.

functions.name: schHiInstToView
functions.description: Generates a cellview from an instance of a symbol. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiMakeCell
functions.description: Starts the schematic Make Cell command. Make Cell cuts out a rectangular region of the schematic, moving it into a new schematic cellview, and fills in the gap with a new hierarchical instance. The command adjusts the design hierarchy without changing the connectivity. You can define the rectangular area you wish to cut.

functions.name: schHiMousePopUp
functions.description: Displays a pop-up menu at the location of the cursor. The menu displayed is sensitive to the location of the cursor and the mode of the cellview in the window. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiMove
functions.description: Moves objects to a different location. You can move objects between different schematic and symbol cellviews. Usable when editing schematics or symbols. Partially selected objects cannot be moved to a different cellview. Does not support change in orientation for partially selected objects.

functions.name: schHiNetExprAvailProps
functions.description: Displays the Net Expression Available Property Names form. Use this form to find the net expression property names that are available for setting on the selected instances.

functions.name: schHiNetExprEvalNames
functions.description: Displays the Net Expression Evaluated Names form. Use this form to view the net names that result from the evaluation of all net expressions that are found in the hierarchy below the selected instances.

functions.name: schHiNewCellView
functions.description: Displays the Create New File form. This function needs to be invoked from a window that contains either schematic or symbol data.

functions.name: schHiObjectProperty
functions.description: Displays a form that lets you modify the properties of selected objects. Usable only when editing a schematic or symbol cellview.

functions.name: schHiOpenCellView
functions.description: Displays the Open File form. You specify the library name, cell name, view name, and edit mode in this form. The specified cellview is displayed in the current window. Usable for opening schematic and symbol design windows.

functions.name: schHiOpenOtherView
functions.syntax: schHiOpenOtherView( d_cellViewID  [ t_viewNames ]  [ w_windowID ] [ w_sessionWindowID ] ) => nil / windowID
functions.description: Allows you to switch between schematic and symbol views.

functions.name: schHiOpenSymbolOrSchematicView
functions.description: Takes the current viewtype, schematic or symbol, then calls schHiOpenOtherView to then switch between the views.

functions.name: schHiPinListToView
functions.syntax: schHiPinListToView( [ ?libName t_libName ] [ ?cellName t_cellName ] [ ?viewName t_viewName ] [ ?inPinList t_inPinList ] [ ?outPinList t_outPinList ] [ ?ioPinList t_ioPinList ] [ ?swPinList t_swPinList ] [ ?dataType t_dataType ] [ ?jpPinList t_jpPinList ] [ ?trPinList t_trPinList ] [ ?unPinList t_unPinList ] ) => t
functions.description: Generates a cellview from a pin list. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiPlot
functions.description: Brings up the Submit Plot form to let you generate schematic plots. Usable when viewing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiPlotQueueStatus
functions.description: Displays the plot jobs in the spooling queues. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiRaiseCurrentForm
functions.description: Brings the most recently-used open form to the front. If there are no open forms, the command does nothing. Bound to F3 by default.

functions.name: schHiRegisterWireStubs
functions.description: Invokes the Register Net Name per Terminal form.

functions.name: schHiRenumberAllSheet
functions.description: Sequentially renumbers all sheets in a multisheet schematic. Usable only when editing an index schematic.

functions.name: schHiRenumberInstances
functions.description: Opens the Renumber Instances form which can be used to renumber instances automatically.

functions.name: schHiRenumberSheet
functions.description: Changes the number of a sheet in a multisheet schematic. Changes the cell name of the renumbered schematic to match the destination sheet number. If a sheet already exists with the destination number, the renumbered sheet is inserted before it. All succeeding sheets will be renumbered accordingly.

functions.name: schHiReplace
functions.syntax: schHiReplace( [ ?replaceAll g_replaceAll ] [ ?propName t_propName ] [ ?condOp t_condOp ] [ ?propValue t_propValue ] [ ?newPropName t_newPropName ] [ ?newPropValue t_newPropValue ] ) => t
functions.description: Replaces objects that match the specified search criteria with a specified value. Usable when editing symbols or schematics. You must have write access to each of the cellviews. Only supports matching of strings, integers, floating-point numbers, and time. This function does not support other property types.

functions.name: schHiResetInvisibleLabels
functions.description: Causes the highlighted labels to either remain visible or reverse to the invisible state in the design. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiReturn
functions.description: Returns up the hierarchy. Usable when editing schematics or symbols after completing a descend or edit-in-place action.

functions.name: schHiReturnToTop
functions.description: Returns to the top-level cellview in the hierarchy. Usable when editing schematics or symbols after completing a series of descend commands.

functions.name: schHiRotate
functions.description: Rotates objects. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiRouteFlightLine
functions.description: Routes logical connections shown as flight lines. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiRouteNamedConnection
functions.description: Starts an interactive command for converting existing wire-by-name connections into wired connections.

functions.name: schHiSRC
functions.description: Sets schematic rules checker (SRC) options, and runs the schematic rules checker. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiSaveCellView
functions.description: Saves the design in the current window.

functions.name: schHiSelectAll
